BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r1.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r1.claim: The Mathnawī couplets commend love and companionship with people of heart, whose hidden worth is known to God.
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r1.anchor: قال في "المثنوي" : مهر ا كان درميان جان نشان

BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r2.claim: The encounter verse explains how hypocrites treated believers and unbelievers and prepares the account of their hypocrisy; it is not a repetition.
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r2.anchor: بيان لمعاملتهم مع المؤمنين والكفار وما صدرت به القصة فمساقه لبيان مذهبهم وتمهيد نفاقهم فليس بتكرير

BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r3.claim: The believers they meet are the Muhājirūn and Anṣār, whom the hypocrites falsely greet as though sharing their faith.
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r3.anchor: واستقبلوا الذين آمنوا بالحق وهم المهاجرون والأنصار

BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r4.claim: An account depicts Ibn Ubayy greeting Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAlī with lavish praise, then assuring ʿAlī that his faith matches theirs while feigning Muslim loyalty.
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r4.anchor: روي أن عبد الله بن أبي المنافق وأصحابه خرجوا ذات يوم فاستقبلهم نفر من الصحابة

BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r5.claim: ʿAlī warns Ibn Ubayy against hypocrisy; after the groups part, Ibn Ubayy asks his companions how he handled the encounter and tells them to imitate him.
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r5.anchor: يا عبد الله اتق الله ولا تنافق فإن المنافقين شر خلق الله

BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r6.claim: The phrase about withdrawing to them can mean departing, privately meeting, or being alone; ilā may function like maʿa or bāʾ, as in the idiom for being alone with someone.
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r6.anchor: مضوا أو اجتمعوا على الخلوة وإلى بمعنى مع

BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r7.claim: Their satans are associates who resemble Satan in rebellion and publicly reveal disbelief; the term can also distinguish senior hypocrites from the junior ones who speak.
BURSEVI:v1p46#3/r7.anchor: أصحابهم المماثلين للشيطان في التمرد والعناد المظهرين لكفرهم وإضافتهم إليه للمشاركة في الكفر

BURSEVI:v1p47/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p47/r1.speaker: الضحاك
BURSEVI:v1p47/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies their satans as soothsayers: Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf among Qurayẓa, Abū Burda among Aslam, ʿAbd al-Dār among Juhayna, ʿAwf b. ʿĀmir among Asad, and ʿAbd Allāh b. Sawdāʾ in Syria.
BURSEVI:v1p47/r1.anchor: وقال الضحاك المراد بشياطينهم كهنتهم وهم في بني قريظة

BURSEVI:v1p47/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p47/r2.speaker: الضحاك
BURSEVI:v1p47/r2.claim: Arabs believed soothsayers knew the unseen and secrets and treated the ill; each soothsayer had a satan who supplied divinations, and they were called satans for being far from truth.
BURSEVI:v1p47/r2.anchor: وكانت العرب تعتقد فيهم أنهم مطلعون على الغيب ويعرفون الأسرار ويداوون المرضى

BURSEVI:v1p47/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p47/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p47/r3.claim: The hypocrites’ private claim means they remain companions and agree in religion and belief, never leaving their faction.
BURSEVI:v1p47/r3.anchor: إنا مصاحبوكم وموافقوكم على دينكم واعتقادكم لا نفارقكم في حال من الأحوال

BURSEVI:v1p47/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p47/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p47/r4.claim: Their profession of Islam before believers is only a show: it secures spoils, marriages, intelligence, and protection for their families and property, while they ridicule the believers.
BURSEVI:v1p47/r4.anchor: وإنما نكون معهم ظاهرا لنشاركهم في غنائمهم وننكح بناتهم ونطلع على أسرارهم ونحفظ أموالنا

BURSEVI:v1p47/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p47/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p47/r5.claim: Istehzāʾ means treating someone as ignorant, mocking, or belittling him; the hypocrites say they display Islam only to deride Muḥammad and his Companions.
BURSEVI:v1p47/r5.anchor: والاستهزاء التجهيل والسخرية والاستخفاف والمعنى أنا نجهل محمدا وأصحابه ونسخر بهم

QASHANI:2:14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:14/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:14/r1.claim: The hypocrites retain a weak, nearly extinguished innate light that lets them associate with believers, alongside stronger acquired darkness aligning them with unbelievers.
QASHANI:2:14/r1.anchor: اللازم لحصول استعدادين فيهم الفطري النوري، الضعيف المغلوب، القريب من الانطفاء، الذي ناسبوا به المؤمنين

QASHANI:2:14/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:14/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:14/r2.claim: Shayṭān derives from distance; their devils are deeply distant and expelled, and their leaders have reached great depths in hypocrisy.
QASHANI:2:14/r2.anchor: والشيطان فيعال من الشطون، الذي هو البعد، وشياطينهم المتعمقون في البعد وهم المطرودون، ورؤساؤهم البالغون في النفاق

QASHANI:2:14/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:14/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:14/r3.claim: Their mockery shows darkness is strong and the luminous orientation weak: they belittle what feels insignificant, while light alone reveals light's worth.
QASHANI:2:14/r3.anchor: واستهزاؤهم بالمؤمنين يدل على ضعف جهة النور وقوة جهة الظلمة فيهم، إذ المستخف بالشيء هو الذي يجد ذلك الشيء في نفسه خفيفا، قليل الوزن والقدر

QASHANI:2:14/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:14/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:14/r4.claim: They undervalue luminous people and turn to unbelievers because darkness predominates in them.
QASHANI:2:14/r4.anchor: فهم يستخفون النورانيين لخفة النور عندهم، إذ بالنور يعرف قدر النور، وبرجحان الظلمة فيهم أووا إلى الكفار وألفوهم

AKHFASH:v1p50/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p50/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p50/r1.claim: The plural wāw in لقوا is omitted when its sukūn meets the lām of الذين; the remaining form still signals plurality.
AKHFASH:v1p50/r1.anchor: فذهبت لسكونه ولم تحتج الى حركته لان فيما بقي دليلا على الجمع

AKHFASH:v1p50/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p50/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p50/r4.claim: خلوت إلى فلان في حاجة can mean the same as خلوت بفلان, but the latter can also mean mocking him.
AKHFASH:v1p50/r4.anchor: له معنيان احدهما هذا والآخر سخرت به

AKHFASH:v1p50/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p50/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p50/r5.claim: The preposition إلى can mean مع, as in من أنصاري إلى الله.

AKHFASH:v1p50/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p50/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p50/r6.claim: Prepositions can shift sense: من may mean على, باء may mean على, and في may mean على.
AKHFASH:v1p50/r6.anchor: كما كانت "من" في معنى (على) في قوله {ونصرناه من القوم}

AKHFASH:v1p50/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p50/r7.speaker: يونس
AKHFASH:v1p50/r7.claim: Yunus reports that Arabs use في أبيك for عليه, ظفرت عليه for به, and رضيت عليه for عنه.
AKHFASH:v1p50/r7.anchor: وزعم يونس ان العرب تقول: "نزلت في أبيك" تريد "عليه"

AKHFASH:v1p50/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p50/r8.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p50/r8.claim: An anonymous poetic example uses علي after رضيت to show the preposition's shifted sense.
AKHFASH:v1p50/r8.anchor: اذا رضيت علي بنو قشير * لعمر الله أعجبني رضاها

NAHHAS:v1p189/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p189/r8.claim: The form لقيوا loses the yāʾ’s damma for heaviness, then drops the yāʾ where two sukūns meet.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r8.anchor: الأصل لقيوا حذفت الضمة من الياء لثقلها ثم حذفت الياء لالتقاء الساكنين

NAHHAS:v1p189/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r9.speaker: محمد بن السميفع اليماني
NAHHAS:v1p189/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa al-Yamani read لاقوا, whose underlying form is لاقيوا.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r9.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن السميفع اليماني ( وإذا لاقوا الذين آمنوا ) والأصل لاقيوا

NAHHAS:v1p189/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p189/r10.claim: In connected speech لقوا drops the vowel before wāw because it is already indicated; لاقوا keeps its vowel because the preceding letter is fatḥa.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r10.anchor: فحذفت لالتقاء الساكنين وحركت في لاقوا لأن قبلها فتحة

NAHHAS:v1p189/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p189/r11.claim: Alladhina is accusative as the object of آمنوا, which is inside its relative clause; قالوا آمنا answers إذا.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r11.anchor: الذين في موضع نصب بالفعل آمنوا داخل في الصلة ( قالوا آمنا ) جواب إذا

NAHHAS:v1p189/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p189/r12.claim: With a softened hamza in شياطينهم, its vowel transfers to wāw and the hamza is deleted, as in the Medinan reading.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r12.anchor: فإن خففت الهمزة ألقيت حركتها على الواو وحذفتها كما يقرأ أهل المدينة شياطينهم

NAHHAS:v1p189/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p189/r13.claim: Shayatin is genitive after إلى; its broken plural keeps its nūn in construct, while the suffix is genitive by annexation.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r13.anchor: شياطينهم خفض بإلى وهو جمع مكسر فلذلك لم تحذف منه النون بالإضافة

NAHHAS:v1p189/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p189/r14.claim: The underlying إنا is إننا, shortened to avoid successive nūns; معكم is accusative through an implied state of being.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r14.anchor: الأصل إننا حذفت منه لاجتماع النونات معكم نصب بالاستقرار

NAHHAS:v1p189/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p189/r15.claim: Those who give ʿayn sukun treat مع as a preposition.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r15.anchor: ومن أسكن العين جعل مع حرفا

NAHHAS:v1p189/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p189/r16.claim: إنما نحن مستهزءون is a nominal sentence; Sibawayh softens its hamza between hamza and wāw because its vowel belongs there.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r16.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر فإن خففت الهمزة فسيبويه يجعلها بين الهمزة والواو

NAHHAS:v1p189/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r17.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p189/r17.claim: Al-Akhfash instead makes the softened hamza a pure yāʾ, yielding مستهزيون, by analogy with his treatment of السفهاء.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r17.anchor: وزعم الأخفش أنه يجعلها ياءا محضة فيقول ( مستهزيون

NAHHAS:v1p189/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r18.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v1p189/r18.claim: Ibn Yazid rejects al-Akhfash’s analogy: السفهاء requires wāw after softening toward alif, while مستهزئون has no such constraint.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r18.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد ليس كما قال الأخفش لأن قوله السفهاء إلا لو جئت بها بين بين

NAHHAS:v1p189/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p189/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p189/r19.claim: A reader who replaces the hamza says مستهزون; this is the form written in the codex.
NAHHAS:v1p189/r19.anchor: ومن أبدل الهمزة قال مستهزون وعلى هذا كتبت في المصحف

IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r1.claim: Some Jews told the Prophet’s companions, when they met them, that they followed the companions’ religion.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : واذا لقوا الذين امنوا قالوا امنا قال كان رجال من اليهود

IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r2.claim: The Jews characterized Muhammad as the companions’ messenger, but said his message was specifically for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : واذا لقوا الذين امنو قالوا امنا اي صاحبكم رسول الله ، ولكنه اليكم خاصة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r3.claim: The verb khala means that they went away.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r3.anchor: عن السدى ، عن أبي مالك ، قوله : خلو يعني مضوا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : واذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم وهم اخوانهم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r5.claim: The devils were Jewish leaders who urged them to deny and oppose what the Messenger brought.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس : واذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم من يهود الذين يامرونهم بالتكذيب وخلاف ما جاء به الرسول

IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r6.claim: Their devils were their leaders and chiefs in associating partners with God and in evil.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : واذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم قال : إلى رؤسائهم وقادتهم في الشرك والشر

IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r7.claim: Their devils were their associates among the hypocrites and polytheists.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد : واذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم إلى اصحابهم من المناقفين والمشركين

IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r8.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r8.claim: The author identifies the devils as Jewish leaders, including Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, and notes that Abu al-ʿAliya, al-Suddi, and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas explained it similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p46/r8.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وكذا فسره أبو العالية والسدى والربيع بن انس

IBNABIHATIM:v1p48/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p48/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p48/r1.claim: By saying they were with the hypocrites, they meant they followed the same religion as them.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p48/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قالوا انا معكم اي انا على مثل ما أنتم عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p48/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p48/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p48/r2.claim: Their claim that they were joking meant they were mocking Muhammad’s companions; Qatada and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas report the same explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p48/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قالوا انا معكم ، انما نحن مستهزئون ساخرون باصحاب محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وروى عن قتادة والربيع بن انس نحو ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r5.claim: The meeting clause is coordinated with the preceding clauses about being told not to spread corruption and to believe like others.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r6.claim: Meeting believers sets up the main disclosure: hypocrites perform sincerity before them, then reveal their real allegiance when alone with their leaders.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r6.anchor: المقصود هنا وصف ما كانوا يعملون مع المؤمنين وإيهامهم أنهم منهم ولقائهم بوجوه الصادقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r7.claim: Amanā means they claimed to have become believers in the legal-religious sense; the more apparent reading needs no omitted object, unlike the alternative that they believed what the believers believed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r7.anchor: الإيمان الشرعي الذي هو مجموع الأوصاف الاعتقادية والعلمية التي تلقب بها المؤمنون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r8.claim: They only outwardly professed faith: they spoke Islam's formula and other words signifying belief without inward conviction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p288#2/r8.anchor: أظهروا أنهم مؤمنون بمجرد القول لا بعقد القلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r1.claim: The clause about withdrawing to their devils is the main point; meeting believers prepares for it, so this adds behavior beyond the general claim in 2:8.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r1.anchor: وذلك ظاهر من السياق لأن كل أحد يعلم أن المقصود أنهم يقولون آمنا في حال استهزاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r2.claim: The two coordinated clauses independently enumerate hypocrites' failings; neither is made circumstantial, since each is a self-contained sign and the clauses match in form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r2.anchor: قصد بالعطف استقلال كلتيهما لأن الغرض تعداد مساويهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r3.claim: In its literal sense Satan is a fiery, subtle creature among the jinn, as the Qur'an says of Iblis; figuratively it means a corrupter or instigator of evil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r3.anchor: وحقيقة الشيطان أنه نوع من المخلوقات المجردة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r4.claim: Here devils figuratively names the hypocrites' leaders in hypocrisy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r4.anchor: وكذلك أطلق هنا على قادة المنافقين في النفاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r5.speaker: البصريون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r5.claim: Basran grammarians derive shayṭān as fayʿāl from shatana, meaning to be distant, with an original nūn because Satan is distant from God's mercy and Paradise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r5.anchor: فقال البصريون هو فيعال من شطن بمعنى بعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r6.speaker: الكوفيون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r6.claim: Kufan grammarians derive shayṭān as faʿlān from shāṭa, meaning to flare, burn, or perish, with an added nūn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r6.anchor: وقال الكوفيون هو فعلان من شاط بمعنى هاج أو احترق أو بطل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r7.claim: The dispute concerns the word's derivational form, not how it declines; its tanwīn in 15:17 conflicts with treating it like an adjective such as ghaḍbān.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r7.anchor: وإلا فإنه لا يظن بنحاة الكوفة أن يدعوا أنه يعامل معاملة الوصف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya argues that Sibawayh's reported Arabic verb tashayṭana points to derivation from shatana rather than shāṭa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية ويرد على قول الكوفيين أن سيبويه حكى أن العرب تقول تشيطن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r9.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r9.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports that Sibawayh treated the nūn of shayṭān as original in one passage and extra in another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p289/r9.anchor: جعل سيبويه نون شيطان في موضع من كتابه أصلية وفي آخر زائدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r1.claim: The verb tashayṭana does not settle the etymology: speakers formed it from the noun and retained that noun's letters, treating it like a fixed name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r1.anchor: تشيطن لما كان وصفا مشتقا من الاسم كقولهم تنمر أثبتوا فيه حروف الاسم على ما هي عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r2.claim: He proposes that shayṭān is a fixed loanword from an earlier language, noting similar terms across ancient languages and a reported Persian form, sīṭān.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r2.anchor: وعندي أنه اسم جامد شابه في حروفه مادة مشتقة ودخل في العربية من لغة سابقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r3.claim: Khalaw means to be alone; its prepositions vary, while ilā here implies returning to one's usual refuge and makes meetings with believers sound brief and incidental.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r3.anchor: ويعدى بإلى على تضمين معنى آب أو خلص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r4.claim: The differing levels of emphasis suit each audience: their unqualified claim to believers avoids alerting them to doubt, while reassurance to leaders answers suspicions created by their performance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p290/r4.anchor: فخلو خطابهم مع المؤمنين عما يفيد تأكيد الخبر لأنهم لا يريدون أن يعرضوا أنفسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r1.claim: They emphasize that they remain with their leaders because their careful display before Muslims could make the leaders suspect a genuine conversion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r1.anchor: لما بدا من إبداعهم في النفاق عند لقاء المسلمين ما يوجب شك كبرائهم في البقاء على الكفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r2.claim: In inna ma naḥnu mustahziʾūn, the restriction is an emphatic reversal: they are only mocking, not sincere believers, and it confirms their allegiance to the leaders.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r2.anchor: قصروا أنفسهم على الاستهزاء قصرا إضافيا للقلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that they omit emphasis before believers because they claim only a new conversion, which they know will not persuade; they emphasize to leaders because the claim matters and will be believed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r3.anchor: بأن مخاطبتهم المؤمنين انتفى عنها ما يقتضي تأكيد الخبر لأن المخبرين لم يتعلق غرضهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r4.claim: The second statement may answer an imagined objection about reconciling their allegiance with their Muslim-facing conduct, or serve as an encompassing apposition to the first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r4.anchor: كأن سائلا يعجب من دعوى بقائهم على دينهم لما أتقنوه من مظاهر النفاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r5.claim: He prefers the explanatory restart: it both reinforces their first claim and resolves the audience's puzzlement, a benefit lost if the clause is merely emphasis or apposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p291/r5.anchor: والوجه الأول أولى الوجوه لأنه يجمع ما تفيده البدلية والتأكيد من تقرير مضمون الجملة الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r4.claim: The form liqaw derives from liqiyū, with the yāʾ dropped after the vowel was lightened; Ibn al-Sumayfa reads “lāqaw.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r4.anchor: أصله لقيوا استثقلت الضمة على الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r5.claim: Hypocrites professed Islam before believers and showed disbelief in private; kinship clouded proof, while their public profession protected their lives and the Prophet refrained from killing them lest people say he killed his companions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r5.anchor: دعه لا يتحدث الناس أن محمدا يقتل أصحابه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r6.claim: When ʿUmar urged killing ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy after his “honorable” and “humiliated” remark, the Prophet told him to leave the man alive to avoid that public accusation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#2/r6.anchor: لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r1.speaker: أصحاب مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r1.claim: The Maliki position explains the Prophet's restraint despite knowing the hypocrites' general disbelief as a precedent that a judge does not rule from private knowledge; it cites the warning in 33:60–61 if they openly manifest hypocrisy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r1.anchor: الحاكم لا يحكم بعلمه إذ لم يشهد على المنافقين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r2.claim: He interprets the threat against hypocrites as applying when they openly declare their hypocrisy.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r3.claim: Malik equates the hypocrite of the Prophet's era with the present-day zindīq and says a zindīq is executed on testimony without an opportunity to repent, since he conceals what would be repented of.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r3.anchor: النفاق في عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هو الزندقة فينا اليوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r4.speaker: إسماعيل القاضي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r4.claim: He says only Zayd b. Arqam testified against ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy and only ʿUmayr b. Saʿd against al-Jullās; two witnesses to either man's disbelief or hypocrisy would have led to execution.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r4.anchor: لم يشهد على عبد الله بن أبي إلا زيد بن أرقم وحده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r5.claim: He argues the testimony was not explicit proof of disbelief; rather, disbelief was inferred from the force of the words, making this stronger than the mere fact that one witness stood alone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r5.anchor: اللفظ ليس بصريح كفر وإنما يفهم من قوته الكفر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r6.speaker: الشافعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says an accused zindīq who denies the charge, openly professes Islam, and disavows other religions is not to be killed; the Ahl al-Raʾy and al-Ṭabarī agree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r6.anchor: السنة فيمن شهد عليه بالزندقة فجحد وأعلن بالإيمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r7.speaker: الشافعي وأصحابه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r7.claim: They explain that outward Islam erased what preceded it, as it did for the Prophet's hypocrites; imposing harsher treatment on zindīqs conflicts with Qurʾān and Sunna and elevates witness testimony above God's testimony about hypocrites.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p94#3/r7.anchor: ما يظهرونه يجب ما قبله فمن قال إن عقوبة الزنادقة أشد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r1.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة وابن حنبل وأهل الحديث
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r1.claim: They say the Prophet was barred from killing hypocrites who outwardly professed Islam and prayed; the same rule applies to a zindīq.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r1.anchor: أن الله تعالى نهاه عن قتلهم إذا أظهروا الإيمان وصلوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r2.speaker: ابن حنبل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r2.claim: He cites the report of ʿUbayd Allāh b. ʿAdī from an Anṣārī about a man accused of hypocrisy: the Prophet asked whether he testified to the two testimonies and prayed, then said these were people God forbade him to kill.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r3.speaker: أهل الحديث
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r3.claim: They also transmit the Prophet's hope that descendants of the hypocrites would believe in God, affirm the messengers, and devote worship sincerely to the Lord of all worlds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r3.anchor: لعل الله سيخرج من أصلابهم من يؤمن بالله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says legal judgments concern outward conduct, while God alone judges hidden states; the Prophet treated hypocrites as Muslims according to their profession, despite God's disclosure of their lying in 63:1.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r4.anchor: قد جعل الأحكام بين عباده على الظاهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r5.claim: The Malikis answer that 63:1 rebukes anyone suspected of hypocrisy generally without identifying individuals; each could deny being its subject, so it did not expose a particular person's lie in a way that canceled his profession.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r5.anchor: لم تعين أشخاصهم وإنما جاء فيها توبيخ لكل مغموض عليه بالنفاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r6.claim: Khala is normally joined to bi, but here ilā follows it because khala means “went away,” parallel to liqaw; al-Farazdaq's verse likewise uses a verb meaning to turn or depart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p95/r6.anchor: وصلت خلوا ب إلى وعرفها أن توصل بالباء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r1.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r1.claim: Makkī says khala bi-flān can mean to mock him, so the verse's ilā removes the possible ambiguity associated with bi.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r1.anchor: يقال خلوت بفلان بمعنى سخرت به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r2.claim: Some take ilā to mean maʿa (“with”); Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this weak and points ahead to 3:52 and 61:14.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r2.anchor: وفي هذا ضعف ويأتي بيانه إن شاء الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r3.claim: Some say ilā substitutes for bi because particles can replace one another; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this as weak and contrary to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r3.anchor: وهذا ضعيف يأباه الخليل وسيبويه وغيرهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the hypocrites' satans as the leaders of disbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r4.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه: «هم رؤساء الكفر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r5.speaker: ابن الكلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r5.claim: Ibn al-Kalbī and others identify the satans as jinn; Ibn ʿAṭiyya regards that as unlikely in this context.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r6.speaker: جمع من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r6.claim: A group of commentators say the satans are soothsayers; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the term's sense of distance from faith and good can encompass all these groups and the hypocrites themselves.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r7.claim: “We are only mocking” means they regard the believers whom they flatter by professing faith as objects of ridicule and contempt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r7.anchor: نتخذ هؤلاء الذين نصانعهم بإظهار الإيمان هزوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r8.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r8.claim: Sībawayh writes the hamza of mustahziʾūn with ḍamma over wāw; Abū ʿAlī reports his allowance of a softened hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r8.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه رحمه الله أن تكون الهمزة مضمومة على الواو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r9.speaker: الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r9.claim: Al-Akhfash reads mustahziyun by turning the hamza into a full yāʾ; Ibn Jinnī explains its ḍamma as recalling the original hamza, since Arabs dislike a yāʾ with ḍamma after kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r9.anchor: أن تقلب الهمزة ياء قلبا صحيحا فيقرأ «مستهزيون»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r10.claim: Most reciters follow Sībawayh's form; haziʾa and istahzaʾa are synonymous, like ʿajiba and istaʿjaba, and Aws b. Ḥajar's verse illustrates the latter form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p96/r10.anchor: وأكثر القراء على ما ذهب إليه سيبويه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي وأصحابه قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says it concerns hypocrites and some People of the Book who professed faith before the Prophet but contradicted it before their leaders.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r2.anchor: في المنافقين وغيرهم من أهل الكتاب الذين كانوا يظهرون للنبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r3.claim: Here ilā means maʿa, “with,” as in the verse about helpers “to God.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r3.anchor: فأما التفسير ف لى بمعنى مع كقوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r4.claim: One etymology derives shayṭān from shatana, “to be far from good,” making nūn part of the root; Umayya’s shāṭin and al-Nābigha’s shaṭūn attest the sense of distance or rebellion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r4.anchor: أنه من شطن أي بعد عن الخير فعلى هذا تكون النون أصلية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r5.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r5.claim: Umayya uses shāṭin of a rebellious being, supporting the derivation from distance from good.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r5.anchor: أيما شاطن عصاه عكاه ثم يلقى في السجن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r6.speaker: النابغة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r6.claim: Al-Nābigha uses shaṭūn for something distant, supporting the same etymology.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r6.anchor: نأت بسعاد عنك نوى شطون فبانت والفؤاد بها رهين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r7.claim: A second etymology derives shayṭān from shāṭa, “to blaze or burn,” making nūn an added letter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r7.anchor: أنه من شاط يشيط إذا التهب واحترق فتكون النون زائدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r8.claim: The verse of poetry “وقد يشيط على أرماحنا البطل” uses yashīṭ to mean “perishes,” illustrating the second derivation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r8.anchor: وقد يشيط على أرماحنا البطل أي يهلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi identify their satans as leaders in unbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r9.anchor: انهم رؤوسهم في الكفر قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r10.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r10.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya and Mujahid identify their satans as their polytheist brethren.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r10.anchor: إخوانهم من المشركين قاله أبو العالية ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r11.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p34#2/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi identify their satans as their soothsayers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p35/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p35/r1.claim: “We are with you” can mean sharing the same religion or offering support and assistance; huzwa means mockery.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p35/r1.anchor: الثاني إنا معكم على النصرة والمعاضدة والهزء السخرية

JISHUMI:v1p255/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p255/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p255/r1.claim: The transmitted reading is لقوا; a variant لاقوا has the same sense, but recitation must follow what is widely transmitted from the Prophet and Companions.
JISHUMI:v1p255/r1.anchor: ظاهر القراءة لقوا وعن بعضهم لاقوا والمعنى واحد

JISHUMI:v1p255/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p255/r2.speaker: الخليل
JISHUMI:v1p255/r2.claim: Meeting is the opposite of being screened; fundamentally it is two things encountering one another face to face.
JISHUMI:v1p255/r2.anchor: قال الخليل: كل شيء استقبل شيئا وصادفه فقد لقيه

JISHUMI:v1p255/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p255/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p255/r3.claim: خلا is the opposite of being among others; mockery and derision are synonyms of jest, while seriousness is their opposite.
JISHUMI:v1p255/r3.anchor: والهزء والسخرية بمعنى، ونظيره الهزل، ونقيضه الجد.

JISHUMI:v1p255/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p255/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v1p255/r4.claim: He defines Satan as any rebellious being among jinn, humans, or animals; another lexicographer defines one as rebellious from any species.
JISHUMI:v1p255/r4.anchor: الشيطان: كل عات متمرد من الجن والإنس والدواب، عن أبي عبيدة

JISHUMI:v1p255/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p255/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p255/r5.claim: Two etymologies are offered: Satan may be distant from good (form fayʿāl) or associated with burning (form faʿlān); the verb means becoming satan-like.
JISHUMI:v1p255/r5.anchor: وأصله من. شطن إذا بعد، كأنه بعد عن الخير، ووزنه فيعال، وقيل: هو من الشيط

JISHUMI:v1p255/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p255/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p255/r6.claim: لقوا derives from لقيوا, with the vowel moved and adjacent silent letters resolved by deleting the wāw.
JISHUMI:v1p255/r6.anchor: لقوا أصله: لقيوا فاستثقلت الضمة على الياء، فنقلت إلى القاف

JISHUMI:v1p255/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p255/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p255/r7.claim: إلى may mean ‘with,’ as in 3:52 and an Arabic proverb, or mark a destination; here it marks turning from believers to leaders.
JISHUMI:v1p255/r7.anchor: قيل: الذود إلى الذود إبل، عن النضر بن شميل

JISHUMI:v1p255/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p255/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p255/r8.claim: خلوت به can mean mocking someone or being alone with him, whereas خلوت إليه indicates making him the destination of one's need.
JISHUMI:v1p255/r8.anchor: ويقال: خلوت به يحتمل معنيين هزئت به وسخرت، وانفردت به

JISHUMI:v1p255/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p255/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p255/r9.claim: إنا contracts إننا by deleting the second nūn to avoid a doubled consonant; the full form also occurs in Qur'anic usage.
JISHUMI:v1p255/r9.anchor: والأصل في إنا: إننا، حذفت النون استثقالا للتضعيف

JISHUMI:v1p257/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p257/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p257/r1.claim: After the hypocrites said they would remain well as long as the other party lived, the Muslims reported what happened to the Messenger, and God revealed this verse.
JISHUMI:v1p257/r1.anchor: بما جرى فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية.

JISHUMI:v1p257/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p257/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p257/r2.claim: The hypocrites professed belief in what was revealed to Muhammad when they met believers in order to protect their lives and property.

JISHUMI:v1p257/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p257/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p257/r3.claim: ‘Their satans’ means their leaders among disbelievers; al-Jishumī prefers this over jinn because most scholars hold it, it is more natural, and the context excludes soothsayers. Al-Kalbi reports jinn satans.
JISHUMI:v1p257/r3.anchor: قيل: رؤسائهم من الكفار، عن ابن عباس، وقيل: شياطين الجن، عن الكلبي

JISHUMI:v1p257/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p257/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p257/r4.claim: Another report identifies their leaders as five Jews, including Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and Abu Burda.
JISHUMI:v1p257/r4.anchor: قيل: هم خمسة نفر من اليهود: كعب بن الأشرف بالمدينة، وأبو بردة

JISHUMI:v1p257/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p257/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p257/r5.claim: ‘We are with you’ means either that they share their leaders' religion or that they are their supporters.

JISHUMI:v1p257/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p257/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p257/r6.claim: One proposed motive was winning over their leaders; another was mocking the believers and Muhammad's companions by professing faith.
JISHUMI:v1p257/r6.anchor: قيل: استمالتهم لرؤسائهم، عن أبي علي، وقيل: استهزاء بالمؤمنين

JISHUMI:v1p257/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p257/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p257/r7.claim: The verse condemns religious hypocrisy and ostentation, mockery of people of truth, and the grave offense of siding with unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v1p257/r7.anchor: الآية تدل على قبح النفاق في الدين، والتحذير من ذلك، وكذلك الرياء.

SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r1.claim: إذا is accusative as a temporal adverb governed by قالوا, its جواب; لقوا is its clause, and الذين آمنوا is the object while آمنا is quoted speech in the accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r1.anchor: " إذا " منصوب بقالوا الذي هو جواب لها

SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r2.claim: لقوا derives from لقيوا: the radical ya was deleted after its vowel met plural waw, and the preceding kasra became damma; the same pattern occurs in خشوا and حيوا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r2.anchor: وأصل لقوا: لقيوا بوزن شربوا، فاستثقلت الضمة على الياء

SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r3.claim: Fourteen maṣdar forms are listed for لقي: لقيا، لقية، لقاء، لقاءة، لقاءة، لقى، لقى، لقيا، لقيا، لقيا، لقيانا، لقيانا، لقيانة، تلقاء, with differing vowels and gemination.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14/r3.anchor: وقد سمع في مصدر " لقي " أربعة عشر وزنا: لقيا ولقية بكسر الفاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r1.claim: خلا usually takes باء, which can mean solitude or mockery; إلى here is explicit for solitude alone, or خلا includes the sense of صرف and takes إلى.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r1.anchor: وإنما تعدى في هذه الآية بإلى لمعنى بديع، وهو أنه إذا تعدى بالباء

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r2.claim: Another analysis includes the sense of ذهبوا وانصرفوا in خلا; the poet al-Farazdaq's قتل الله زيادا عني illustrates صرفing someone away by killing him.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r2.anchor: أو تضمن معنى ذهبوا وانصرفوا فيكون كقول الفرزدق

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r3.claim: إلى may mean مع, as in the command about not consuming their property alongside your property.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: هي هنا بمعنى مع، كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r4.claim: إلى may instead mean باء; both this and the مع analysis are allowed only by Kufans, while Basrans reject figurative use of prepositions.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: هي بمعنى الباء، وهذان القولان إنما يجوزان عند الكوفيين

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r5.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r5.claim: The sense may be that they left the believers for their devils, with إلى retaining its basic sense; the author says this needs the preceding تضمين analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: المعنى وإذا خلوا من المؤمنين إلى شياطينهم، ف " إلى " على بابها

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r6.claim: خلووا became خلوا when the first waw turned to alif after a vowel and open preceding syllable, then was deleted before plural waw; the fatḥa marks it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r6.anchor: والأصل في خلوا: خلووا، فقلبت الواو الأولى التي هي لام الكلمة ألفا

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r7.claim: شياطين is a broken plural with two proposed patterns, فعاليل or فعالين; its proper inflection uses case vowels, while a rare dialect treats it like a sound masculine plural.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r7.anchor: فوزن شياطين: إما فعاليل أو فعالين على حسب القولين المتقدمين

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r8.claim: A rare reading has الشياطون, paralleling the faulty colloquial plural بساتون.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#2/r8.anchor: وقرئ شاذا: { وما تنزلت به الشياطون } [الشعراء: 210]

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r1.claim: إنا originates as إننا; one nūn is dropped for ease when it meets the nūn of نا. Abu al-Baqa identifies the omitted nūn as the middle one.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r1.anchor: والأصل في إنا: إننا، كقوله تعالى: إننآ سمعنا مناديا

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r2.claim: مع is an annexed noun functioning as a locative predicate: its pronoun is genitive, and the phrase depends on an omitted place adverb; its sense of companionship suggests location, not time.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r2.anchor: و " مع " ظرف والضمير بعده في محل خفض بإضافته إليه وهو الخبر

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r3.claim: مع may not have a silent عين except in poetry; even then it remains an adverb, despite claims that it becomes a preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r3.anchor: واعلم أن " مع " لا يجوز تسكين عينها إلا في شعر كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r4.speaker: يونس والأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r4.claim: When detached from annexation, مع معا is a maqṣūr noun, unlike the analysis of al-Khalil and Sibawayh.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r4.anchor: قولان، الأول قول يونس والأخفش، والثاني قول الخليل وسيبويه

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#3/r5.claim: Detached معا is usually an accusative circumstantial, but can be a predicate, as in the poet's شعباكما معا; it could alternatively be a circumstantial with an omitted predicate.

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r1.claim: إنما نحن مستهزئون is apparently an independent answer to the leaders' implied question, so it has no syntactic position; another view makes it an accusative appositive to إنا معكم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنها لا محل لها من الإعراب لاستئنافها

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r2.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r2.claim: The hamza in مستهزئون is softened to a sound between hamza and waw.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r2.anchor: وهو رأي سيبويه، ومذهب الأخفش قلبها ياء محضة

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r3.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r3.claim: The hamza in مستهزئون is changed into a fully pronounced yāʾ, unlike Sibawayh's between-sounds analysis.

SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r4.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r4.claim: At pause, Hamza omits the written hamza shape in مستهزئون and فمالئون in conformity with the codex spelling.
SAMIN-DURR:2:14#4/r4.anchor: وقد وقف حمزة على " مستهزئون " و

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r1.claim: Their devils are Jews who urge them to disbelieve.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r1.anchor: في شياطينهم قولان : أحدهما : أنهم اليهود , الذين يأمرونهم بالتكذيب , وهو قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r2.claim: Their devils are the leaders among them in unbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r2.anchor: والثاني : رؤوسهم في الكفر , وهذا قول ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r3.claim: One reading takes إلى as مع, meaning they are with their devils, as in the cited verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r3.anchor: مع شياطينهم , فجعل ( إلى ) موضع ( مع ) , كما قال تعالى : ^ { من أنصاري إلى الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r4.speaker: بعض البصريين
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r4.claim: To be alone with someone toward a need can be expressed as خلوْت إلى; خلوْت به can also mean mockery, making this wording more eloquent and literal.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r4.anchor: وهو قول بعض البصريين : أنه يقال خلوت إلى فلان , إذا جعلته غايتك في حاجتك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r5.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r5.claim: The phrase means that the hypocrites returned to their devils.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r5.anchor: وهو قول بعض الكوفيين : أن معناه إذا انصرفوا إلى شياطينهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r6.claim: Shayṭān may derive from shatana, to be far away: either far from good or far in its evil path; on this derivation the ن is root-letter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r6.anchor: أنه فيعال من شطن , أي بعد , ومنه قولهم : نوى شطون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r7.claim: Another derivation connects shayṭān to shāṭa, to perish; the cited line uses يشيط for perishing, and ن is then an added letter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r7.anchor: أنه مشتق من شاط يشيط , أي هلك يهلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r8.claim: The decisive derivation makes shayṭān a faʿlān from burning, naming it for its eventual state.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r8.anchor: والقول الفاصل : أنه فعلان من الشيط وهو الاحتراق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r9.claim: Their claim of being with the believers means they share the leaders' disbelief and hostility; calling themselves mockers means their displayed assent is feigned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p76/r9.anchor: أي على ما أنتم عليه من التكذيب والعداوة , { إنما نحن مستهزئون } أي ساخرون

MUJAHID:v1p69/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p69/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p69/r1.claim: He identifies the hypocrites' devils as their companions among the hypocrites and polytheists.
MUJAHID:v1p69/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله عز وجل ﴿ وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم ﴾ أصحابهم المنافقين والمشركين

MUQATIL:2:14-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:14-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:14-15/r1.claim: The believers are the Prophet’s Companions who affirmed Muhammad; the hypocrites privately tell Jewish leaders Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf and his followers that they share their religion and feign faith only to mock Muhammad and his Companions.
MUQATIL:2:14-15/r1.anchor: يعنى صدقوا من أصحاب النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم، { قالوا } لهم: { آمنا } صدقنا بمحمد،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r1.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa reads lāqū rather than laqū; both forms mean meeting someone nearby face to face.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة رحمه الله و إذا لاقوا يقال لقيته ولاقيته إذا استقبلته قريبا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r2.claim: The hypocrites feign friendly faces and claim belief when meeting believers while mocking them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r2.anchor: في بيان ما كانوا يعملون مع المؤمنين من الاستهزاء بهم ولقائهم بوجوه المصادقين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r3.claim: Khala ilayhi means being alone with someone; ilayhi marks both departure from believers and arrival among their leaders.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r3.anchor: خلوت بفلان وإليه إذا انفردت معه وبالى أبلغ لأن فيه دلالة الإبتداء والإنتهاء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r4.claim: Their satanic leaders are rebellious people like devils, identified either as Jewish leaders or as anyone resembling devils in rebellion.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r4.anchor: وشياطينهم الذين ماثلوا الشياطين في تمردهم وهم اليهود

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r5.speaker: سيبويه
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r5.claim: Sībawayh says the nūn in shayāṭīn is original, citing the verb tashayṭana.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r5.anchor: وعن سيبويه أن نون الشياطين أصلية بدليل قولهم تشيطن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r6.speaker: سيبويه
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r6.claim: Sībawayh also gives the alternative that shayāṭīn derives from shatana, to be distant from right conduct and truth.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r6.anchor: وعنه أنها زائدة واشتقاقه من شطن إذا بعد لبعده من الصلاح والخبر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r7.claim: A further derivation connects the word to shāṭa, meaning to perish; al-bāṭil is among its names.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r7.anchor: أو من شاط إذا بطل ومن أسمائه الباطل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r8.claim: They tell the believers they are companions and agree with them, then tell their own leaders with emphatic certainty that they remain with them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r8.anchor: إنا مصاحبوكم وموافقوكم على دينكم و إنما خاطبوا المؤمنين بالجملة الفعلية وشياطينهم بالإسمية محققة بأن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r9.claim: Their claim to believers is unconvincing because their convictions do not motivate it and emphasis would not persuade people surrounded by the Emigrants and Helpers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r9.anchor: لأن انفسهم لا تساعدهم عليه إذ ليس لهم من عقائدهم باعث ومحرك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r10.claim: Among their own faction, affirmation suits their desire and is accepted, so it is emphatic.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r10.anchor: فقد كان عن رغبة وقد كان متقبلا منهم رائجا عنهم فكان مظنة للتحقيق ومئنة للتأكيد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r11.claim: Their claim that they only mock Islam confirms their loyalty to Judaism and rejects Islam, since mockery treats its object as invalid.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r11.anchor: تأكيد لقوله إنا معكم لأن معناه الثبات على اليهودية وقوله إنما نحن مستهزئون رد للاسلام ودفع له

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r12.claim: The statement can also be a fresh reply to an objection: if you are with us, why agree with the believers? They answer that they are only mocking.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r12.anchor: أو استئناف كأنهم اعترضوا عليهم بقولهم حين قالوا لهم إنا معكم إن كنتم معنا فلم توافقون المؤمنين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r13.claim: Istihzāʾ means mockery and contempt; its root connotes lightness, from a word for rapid killing.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p19#3/r13.anchor: والاستهزاء السخرية والاستخفاف وأصل الباب الخفة من الهزء وهو القتل السريع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r1.anchor: أنزلت هذه الآية في ذكر المنافقين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r2.speaker: محمد بن السميقع اليماني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r2.claim: He reads لاقوا; its underlying form is لاقيوا, with the vowel change and deletion caused by two adjoining quiescent letters.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r2.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن السميقع اليماني: «لاقوا الذين آمنوا».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r3.claim: The waw remains in لاقوا because a fatḥa precedes it, while it is dropped in لقوا because a preceding ḍamma makes another ḍamma heavy on the tongue.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r3.anchor: لثقلها، وحركت في لاقوا لأن قبلها فتحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r4.claim: Here خلوا means they went away or departed, which explains its construction with إلى; al-Farazdaq's use of صرف supports this sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r4.anchor: «خلوا» هنا بمعنى ذهبوا وانصرفوا ومنه قول الفرزدق:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r5.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r5.claim: Some interpret إلى as مع, though al-Qurṭubī considers this weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r5.anchor: وقال قوم: «إلى» بمعنى مع وفيه ضعف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r6.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r6.claim: Some take إلى to mean باء, but al-Khalil and Sibawayh reject that interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: «إلى» بمعنى الباء وهذا يأباه الخليل وسيبويه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r7.claim: Another reading takes إلى literally: they withdrew from the believers to their devils.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r7.anchor: وقيل: المعنى وإذا خلوا من المؤمنين إلى شياطينهم ف «إلى» على بابها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r8.claim: They identify the devils as the leaders of disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r8.anchor: فقال ابن عباس والسدي: هم رؤساء الكفر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r9.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r9.claim: He identifies the devils as jinn.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r10.speaker: جمع من المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r10.claim: A group of commentators identify them as soothsayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r10.anchor: وقال جمع من المفسرين: هم الكهان.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r11.claim: The word's sense of distance from faith and good encompasses all the groups named.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r11.anchor: ولفظ الشيطنة الذي معناه البعد عن الإيمان والخير يعم جميع من ذكر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r12.claim: مستهزئون means they deny what they are summoned to believe.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r13.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r13.claim: Another interpretation is that they are mocking or scoffing.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r14.claim: The root هزء denotes mockery and play; the rajaz line illustrates هزئت.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r14.anchor: والهزء: السخرية واللعب يقال: هزىء به واستهزأ قال الراجز:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r15.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r15.claim: A further etymology makes استهزاء mean taking vengeance, illustrated by a line from another poet.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:14/r15.anchor: وقيل: أصل الاستهزاء: الانتقام كما قال الآخر:

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r1.claim: This is the fourth kind of their reprehensible conduct; Abu Hanifa reads laqū as lāqaw, and laqiya or lāqiya means to encounter someone face to face.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r1.anchor: هذا هو النوع الرابع من أفعالهم القبيحة ، يقال : لقيته ولاقيته إذا استقبلته قريبا منه ، وقرأ أبو حنيفة : ( وإذا لاقوا )

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r2.claim: Their claim “we believed” means inward, sincere belief: verbal profession was already known, and their claim to believers reverses the inward denial they professed to their leaders.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r2.anchor: إنما المشكوك فيه هو الإخلاص بالقلب ، فيجب أن يكون مرادهم من هذا الكلام ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r3.claim: Khalaw ilayhim can mean being alone with them, departing to them, or privately mocking them; the verse describes carrying and recounting the mockery to their leaders.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r3.anchor: فقال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : يقال خلوت بفلان وإليه ، وإذا انفردت معه

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r4.claim: Their “devils” are people who resemble devils in rebelliousness; they are the senior figures capable of causing corruption on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r4.anchor: فهم الذين ماثلوا الشياطين في تمردهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r5.claim: If “their devils” means senior hypocrites, junior hypocrites tell believers they believe but reassure those leaders that they remain with them; if it means unbelievers, the claim may come from all hypocrites.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r5.anchor: لأن من يحمل الشياطين على كبار المنافقين يحمل هذا القول على أنه من صغارهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r6.claim: Whether the leaders are unbelievers or senior hypocrites, they are the referents; juniors lack the power to corrupt the land.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r6.anchor: ولا شبهة في أن المراد بشياطينهم أكابرهم ، وهم إما الكفار وإما أكابر المنافقين

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r7.claim: They use a verbal sentence with believers but an emphatic nominal sentence with their own leaders because they only allege beginning to believe, cannot sincerely intensify that claim, or know Muslims would reject a claim of perfect faith; they expect their leaders to accept their confident reassurance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r7.anchor: لأنهم كانوا في ادعاء حدوث الإيمان منهم لا في ادعاء أنهم في الدرجة الكاملة منه

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r8.claim: Mockery originally conveys lightness or rapid movement; here it is showing agreement while concealing harm and ridicule.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r8.anchor: وحده أنه عبارة عن إظهار موافقة مع إبطان ما يجري مجرى السوء على طريق السخرية

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r9.claim: They outwardly agree with Islam to avoid harm, discover believers’ secrets, and obtain their charity and spoils.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r9.anchor: لنأمن شرهم ونقف على أسرارهم ، ونأخذ من صدقاتهم وغنائمهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r10.claim: “We are only mocking” may emphasize their continued disbelief, replace “we are with you” because belittling Islam magnifies unbelief, or answer an imagined objection about why they appear to side with Muslims.
RAZI-FULL:v2p62#2/r10.anchor: هو توكيد له ؛ لأن قوله : { إنا معكم } معناه الثبات على الكفر

STUDYQURAN:2:14/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:14/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:2:14/r1.claim: A hypocrite boasted he could divert the believers, praised Companions before them, then told his own companions to imitate him; the revelation exposed their intent.
STUDYQURAN:2:14/r1.anchor: The occasion given for this revelation involves a hypocrite who boasted to his companions

STUDYQURAN:2:14/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:14/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:14/r2.claim: The hypocrites’ satans are variously understood as their leaders, fellow hypocrites, disbelievers, or inner demons.
STUDYQURAN:2:14/r2.anchor: Here it is usually understood to mean the hypocrites’ leaders, fellow hypocrites, disbelievers, or inner demons

STUDYQURAN:2:14/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:14/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:14/r3.claim: Quranic use of satans can include human beings as well as otherworldly beings, as 6:112 illustrates.
STUDYQURAN:2:14/r3.anchor: At times in the Quran shayāṭīn refers not only to otherworldly creatures, but also to human beings

TAB-FULL:v1p306/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p306/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p306/r1.claim: The hypocrites profess faith to believers to protect their lives, property, and families, then assure their leaders and fellow polytheists that they remain allies and only mock the believers.

TAB-FULL:v1p306/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p306/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p306/r2.claim: Jewish men told the Prophet’s companions they followed their religion, then told their own leaders they were with them and merely mocking.
TAB-FULL:v1p306/r2.anchor: كان رجال من اليهود إذا لقوا أصحاب النبي

TAB-FULL:v1p306/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p306/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p306/r3.claim: Their devils were Jews who urged them to deny the Messenger and oppose his teaching; they then claimed to share their companions’ religion.
TAB-FULL:v1p306/r3.anchor: شياطينهم من يهود الذين يأمرونهم بالتكذيب

TAB-FULL:v1p308/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r1.claim: The hypocrites’ devils are the leading figures in disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r1.anchor: أما شياطينهم، فهم رءوسهم في الكفر

TAB-FULL:v1p308/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r2.claim: Their devils are their chiefs and leaders in evil.

TAB-FULL:v1p308/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r3.claim: In another interpretation, their devils are the polytheists.

TAB-FULL:v1p308/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r4.claim: Their devils are the hypocrites’ companions among the disbelievers.

TAB-FULL:v1p308/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r5.claim: Their devils are their companions among hypocrites and polytheists.

TAB-FULL:v1p308/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r6.claim: Their devils are their brothers from among the polytheists.

TAB-FULL:v1p308/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r7.claim: When believers prospered, hypocrites claimed fellowship with them, but in private they mocked the believers.
TAB-FULL:v1p308/r7.anchor: إذا أصاب المؤمنين رخاء، قالوا إنا نحن معكم

TAB-FULL:v1p310/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r1.claim: The phrase’s devils means the hypocrites’ companions among hypocrites and polytheists.

TAB-FULL:v1p310/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r2.speaker: نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r2.claim: A Basran grammarian says khala ila means private conversation for a particular need, while khala bihi can mean either private need or mockery; ila avoids ambiguity.
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r2.anchor: يقال خلوت إلى فلان، إذا أريد به: خلوت إليه

TAB-FULL:v1p310/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r3.claim: An alternative analysis takes ila to mean with, since Arabic prepositions can substitute for one another; the cited verse uses ila in the sense of with.
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r3.anchor: {من أنصاري إلى الله} [آل عمران: 52] يريد مع الله

TAB-FULL:v1p310/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r4.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r4.claim: The cited line uses ʿalayya to mean ʿannī, illustrating substitution among prepositions.

TAB-FULL:v1p310/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r5.speaker: نحويي أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r5.claim: The Kufan analysis takes the phrase as turning their private attention toward their devils; al-Tabari prefers it because ila has its own proper sense and should not be replaced without proof.
TAB-FULL:v1p310/r5.anchor: وهذا القول عندي أولى بالصواب، لأن لكل حرف من حروف المعاني

TAB-FULL:v2p145/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r1.claim: The verse refers to Israelites who heard God’s word and distorted it after understanding; when they met believers they claimed to believe in Muhammad and his revelation, adopting hypocrites’ ways.
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r1.anchor: يعني بذلك أنهم إذا لقوا الذين صدقوا بالله وبمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v2p145/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r2.claim: Some Jews told Muhammad they believed, then privately asked one another whether to reveal what God had disclosed to them.
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r2.anchor: وذلك أن نفرا من اليهود كانوا إذا لقوا محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا: آمنا

TAB-FULL:v2p145/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r3.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r3.claim: Jewish hypocrites said they believed when they met the Prophet’s companions.
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r3.anchor: يعني المنافقين من اليهود كانوا إذا لقوا أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا آمنا

TAB-FULL:v2p145/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r4.claim: They said they believed in the Prophet, but only for the believers’ benefit.
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r4.anchor: أي بصاحبكم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولكنه إليكم خاصة

TAB-FULL:v2p145/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r5.claim: The people in question were Jews who believed and then became hypocrites.
TAB-FULL:v2p145/r5.anchor: هؤلاء ناس من اليهود آمنوا ثم نافقوا

TABRISI:2:14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r1.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:2:14/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the listed passive forms with initial ḍamma, including qīla and jīʾa.
TABRISI:2:14/r1.anchor: قرأ الكسائي قيل وغيض وسئ وسيئت وحيل وسيق وجيء بضم أوائل ذلك كله

TABRISI:2:14/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r2.speaker: يعقوب
TABRISI:2:14/r2.claim: Yaʿqūb is also reported to use the initial-ḍamma reading for all these forms.

TABRISI:2:14/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r3.speaker: نافع
TABRISI:2:14/r3.claim: Nāfiʿ agrees with the preceding reading for سيء and سيئت.

TABRISI:2:14/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
TABRISI:2:14/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir agrees for سيء, سيئت, حيل, and سيق.
TABRISI:2:14/r4.anchor: وابن عامر فيهما وفي حيل وسيق

TABRISI:2:14/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r5.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:2:14/r5.claim: The remaining readers use kasra throughout the listed forms.

TABRISI:2:14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14/r6.claim: The passive forms have three linguistic realizations: kasra, a hint of ḍamma, and a waw-based form; qīla derives by moving the vowel and changing wāw to yāʾ.
TABRISI:2:14/r6.anchor: في هذه كلها ثلاث لغات الكسر وإشمام الضم وقول بالواو فأما قيل بالكسر

TABRISI:2:14/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14/r7.claim: The hint of ḍamma preserves a trace of the original form while easing pronunciation.
TABRISI:2:14/r7.anchor: وأما الإشمام فلأجل الدلالة على الأصل مع التخفيف

TABRISI:2:14/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14/r9.claim: إذا is temporal and conditional; it functions as an adverb, and its answer governs it rather than the quoted response verb itself.
TABRISI:2:14/r9.anchor: إذا لفظة وضعت للوقت بشرط أن يكون ظرفا زمانيا وفيها معنى الشرط

TABRISI:2:14/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14/r10.claim: In وإذا لقوا, إذا is built because it carries the meaning of في and adheres to it; it can also be spatial, as in خرجت فإذا الناس وقوف.
TABRISI:2:14/r10.anchor: وكذلك قوله: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا

TABRISI:2:14/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14/r11.claim: The expression إنما makes إن non-governing, leaving نحن مبتدأ and مصلحون its predicate; نحن is built like a particle and marked by ḍamma as a plural nominative pronoun.
TABRISI:2:14/r11.anchor: وما في قوله إنما كافة كفت إن عن العلم

TABRISI:2:14/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14/r12.claim: The clause لا تفسدوا في الأرض is parsed as a raised clause understood as something said to them.
TABRISI:2:14/r12.anchor: جملة في موضع رفع على تقدير قيل لهم شيء فهي اسم ما لم يسم

TABRISI:2:14/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14/r13.claim: إلا introduces and opens a self-sufficient statement; it began as لا preceded by interrogative alif, which turns denial into confirmation.
TABRISI:2:14/r13.anchor: إلا كلمة تنبيه وافتتاح للكلام تدخل على كل كلام مكتف بنفسه

TABRISI:2:14#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r1.speaker: بعض القراء
TABRISI:2:14#2/r1.claim: Some readers omit the hamza in مستهزؤون.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r1.anchor: بعض القراء ترك الهمزة من مستهزؤون

TABRISI:2:14#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r2.speaker: أهل الحجاز
TABRISI:2:14#2/r2.claim: The Hijazi reading of خلوا إلى drops the hamza and transfers its vowel to the preceding wāw.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r2.anchor: قراءة أهل الحجاز خلولى حذفوا الهمزة وألقوا حركتها على الواو قبلها

TABRISI:2:14#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r3.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:2:14#2/r3.claim: The other readers leave the wāw unvowelled and pronounce the hamza fully.

TABRISI:2:14#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:14#2/r4.claim: Sībawayh says a hamza may be softened to an intermediate sound in the cited vowel environments.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r4.anchor: قال سيبويه: الهمزة المضمومة المكسور ما قبلها تجعلها إذا خففتها بين بين

TABRISI:2:14#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r5.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:2:14#2/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash instead fully changes the hamza of مستهزيون to yāʾ because of the preceding kasra; he rejects intermediate treatment or wāw because they yield an unparalleled form.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r5.anchor: وذهب الأخفش إلى أن تقلب الهمزة ياء في مستهزيون قلبا صحيحا

TABRISI:2:14#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r6.speaker: الخليل
TABRISI:2:14#2/r6.claim: Al-Khalīl defines meeting as anything encountering or coming across something, originally coming together by proximity.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r6.anchor: قال الخليل: كل شيء استقبل شيئا أو صادفه فقد لقيه

TABRISI:2:14#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14#2/r7.claim: خلوت إليه and خلوت معه mean being alone with someone; خلوت به can also mean mocking him.

TABRISI:2:14#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14#2/r8.claim: يستهزئون means they mock; the same verb-pattern shifts meaning in examples such as يستسخرون, يستقر, and استعلى قرنه.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r8.anchor: ويستهزئون أي يهزءون ومثله يستسخرون أي يسخرون وقر واستقر

TABRISI:2:14#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14#2/r9.claim: إنا is shortened from إننا by dropping the second nūn; معكم is adverbial, meaning settled with you.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r9.anchor: إنا أصله إننا لكن النون حذفت لكثرة النونات والمحذوفة النون الثانية من إن

TABRISI:2:14#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14#2/r10.claim: The accusative construction is illustrated by the poet's expression وريشي منكم وهواي معكم.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r10.anchor: انتصب انتصاب الظروف نحو إنا خلفكم

TABRISI:2:14#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14#2/r11.claim: Hypocrites tell believers that they believe what was sent to Muhammad, then tell their leaders privately that they share their religion and only mock Muhammad's companions.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r11.anchor: أن المنافقين إذا رأوا المؤمنين قالوا آمنا أي صدقنا نحن بما أنزل على محمد

TABRISI:2:14#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:14#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the hypocrites' shayāṭīn as their unbelieving leaders.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r12.anchor: قيل رؤساؤهم من الكفار عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:14#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14#2/r13.claim: Another reported view identifies the shayāṭīn as Jews who instructed the hypocrites to deny the message.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r13.anchor: وقيل هم اليهود الذين أمروهم بالتكذيب

TABRISI:2:14#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r14.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
TABRISI:2:14#2/r14.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir says the shayāṭīn are their soothsayers.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r14.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر الباقر عليه السلام أنهم كهانهم

TABRISI:2:14#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:14#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:14#2/r15.claim: إنما نحن مستهزئون means they claim to be with their leaders in religion and to mock and ridicule Muhammad's companions when professing faith.
TABRISI:2:14#2/r15.anchor: أي على دينكم إنما نحن مستهزءون أي نستهزئ بأصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v1p154/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p154/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p154/r8.claim: The verse was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy: he professed support for Muhammad to Saʿd ibn ʿUbada, then urged his own leaders to cling to ancestral religion.
THALABI:v1p154/r8.anchor: ابن عباس قال: كان عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول الخزرجي عظيم المنافقين

THALABI:v1p154/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p154/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p154/r9.claim: Abdullah ibn Ubayy publicly praised Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali, but after Ali rebuked his hypocrisy he told companions to imitate his double dealing; Muslims reported it to the Prophet and the verse came down.
THALABI:v1p154/r9.anchor: ابن عباس: نزلت هذه الآية في عبد الله بن أبي محتجا به

THALABI:v1p154/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p154/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p154/r10.claim: Here laqu means saw; its older form laqiyu was contracted because the kasra was heavy on ya and the adjacent waw and ya became sukuns.

THALABI:v1p155/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r1.speaker: محمد بن السميقع
THALABI:v1p155/r1.claim: He reads laqu as laqu, with the same meaning.
THALABI:v1p155/r1.anchor: محمد بن السميقع: وإذا لاقوا وهما بمعنى واحد

THALABI:v1p155/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p155/r2.claim: The believers whom the hypocrites meet are Abu Bakr and his companions, to whom they say they believe as they do.
THALABI:v1p155/r2.anchor: الذين آمنوا: يعني أبا بكر وأصحابه قالوا آمنا

THALABI:v1p155/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p155/r3.claim: Khala means they returned; khala bihi, ilayhi, and maʿahu all mean being alone with someone.
THALABI:v1p155/r3.anchor: رجعوا، ويجوز أن تكون من الخلوة، تقول: خلوت به وخلوت إليه

THALABI:v1p155/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r4.speaker: النضر بن شميل
THALABI:v1p155/r4.claim: In this construction ila can mean maʿa, as in Qur'anic expressions and two poetic examples.
THALABI:v1p155/r4.anchor: النضر بن شميل: إلى ها هنا بمعنى (مع) كقوله تعالى: أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث إلى نسائكم

THALABI:v1p155/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p155/r5.claim: Their shayatin are their leaders, chiefs, guides, and soothsayers.
THALABI:v1p155/r5.anchor: إلى شياطينهم: أي رؤسائهم وكبرائهم وقادتهم وكهنتهم

THALABI:v1p155/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p155/r6.claim: He identifies five Jewish leaders as their devils: Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf in Medina, Abu Burda among Aslam, Abdullah in Juhayna, Awf ibn Amir among Asad, and Abdullah ibn al-Sawda in Syria.
THALABI:v1p155/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم خمسة نفر من اليهود، ولا يكون كاهن إلا ومعه شيطان

THALABI:v1p155/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p155/r7.claim: Shaytan is any rebellious disobedient being, human or jinn; the term also applies to snakes and troublesome animals.
THALABI:v1p155/r7.anchor: والشيطان: المتمرد العاصي من الجن والإنس، ومن كل شيء

THALABI:v1p155/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p155/r8.claim: A prophetic report calls a rider who crosses before a praying person, then refuses to stop, a devil; another calls a man following a flying pigeon a devil following a devil, meaning a wicked pursuer.
THALABI:v1p155/r8.anchor: إذا مر الرجل بين يدي أحدكم وهو يمتطي فليمنعه

THALABI:v1p155/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r9.speaker: أبو النجم
THALABI:v1p155/r9.claim: His verse jokes that every human poet has a female devil while his own devil is male.
THALABI:v1p155/r9.anchor:
أبو النجم:
إني وكل شاعر من البشر … شيطانه أنثى وشيطاني ذكر

THALABI:v1p155/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p155/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p155/r10.claim: Their assurance إنا معكم means they remain on the leaders' religion and are their supporters; they mock Muhammad and his companions.
THALABI:v1p155/r10.anchor:
قالوا إنا معكم أي على دينكم وأنصاركم.
إنما نحن

ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r1.claim: Zamakhshari and most commentators understand the hypocrites’ “satans” as persistent evildoers who have become like satans.
ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r1.anchor: people "who, through their insolent persistence in evildoing (tamarrud), have become like satans" (Zamakhshari)

ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r2.claim: Asad derives shaytan from remoteness from good and truth, and says the Qur’anic term can describe a person’s own evil impulses, especially those opposed to truth and morality.
