ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r2.anchor: derived from the verb shatana, "he was [or 'became'] remote [from all that is good and true]"

ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r3.speaker: Raghib
ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r3.claim: Raghib explains the term’s Qur’anic use for satanic propensities in the soul, especially impulses contrary to truth and morality.
ASAD-NOTES:2:14#n10/r3.anchor: all impulses which run counter to truth and morality (Raghib)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r1.claim: The believers whom the hypocrites meet are identified as Abū Bakr and his companions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: يعني: أبا بكر -رضي الله عنه- وأصحابه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r2.claim: The form laqū comes from laqiyū; a heavy yāʾ was dropped and its ḍamma transferred to the preceding qāf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r2.anchor: و (لقوا) في الأصل (لقيوا) فاستثقلت الضمة على # (الياء)، فحذفت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r3.speaker: الحراني عن ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt lists the forms liqāʾ, liqyān, liqyā, and laqā for meeting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r3.anchor:
الحراني عن ابن السكيت:
لقيته لقاء ولقيانا ولقيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r4.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r4.claim: Al-Layth says a thing is met when it faces or encounters another thing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r4.anchor: الليث: وكل شيء استقبل شيئا أو صادفه فقد لقيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r5.speaker: النضر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r5.claim: Al-Nadr takes ilā in khalaw ilā as maʿa and cites parallels in 2:187, 3:52 and 61:14, and 4:2.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r6.claim: The grammarians understand the hypocrites as leaving believers and going to their chiefs; the author prefers the ordinary endpoint sense of ilā over treating it as maʿa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r6.anchor: وهذا أحسن من إخراج # (إلى) عن حدها (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r7.claim: A shayṭān is any rebellious, defiant being among jinn or humans, as 6:112 calls human and jinn tempters shayāṭīn.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r7.anchor: والشيطان كل متمرد عات من الجن والإنس (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r8.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r8.claim: Al-Layth derives shayṭān as fayʿāl from shatana, to be distant; he also connects shayṭana with becoming and acting like Satan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r8.anchor: فقال الليث: الشيطان فيعال من شطن أي: بعد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r9.speaker: قوم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r9.claim: Some derive shayṭān as faʿlān from shāṭa, to perish or burn; al-Aʿshā’s verse yushīṭ is cited as evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: الشيطان فعلان من شاط يشيط إذا هلك واحترق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r10.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r10.claim: Abū ʿAlī argues shayṭān is fayʿāl from shatana, not faʿlān from yashīṭ; the following segment gives his morphological evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p164#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو علي: هو (فيعال) من شطن (¬5) مثل: البيطار والغيداق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r1.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects faʿlān because Sibawayh attests shayṭana on the fayʿal pattern; Amiyya’s shāṭin likewise has n as the root’s final radical, establishing shayṭān as fayʿāl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r1.anchor: لأن سيبويه قد حكى: (شيطن) (¬1) وهو (فيعل) لا (فعلن)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r2.claim: Amiyya’s line is decisive: shāṭin is an active participle with n as its final root consonant, so shayṭān is fayʿāl and not faʿlān from yashīṭ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r2.anchor: فكما أن (شاطنا) فاعل، والنون لام، كذلك (شيطان) فيعال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains shayṭān as one extreme in unbelief and far removed from the truth, among jinn or humans.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ومعنى الشيطان: الغالي في الكفر المتبعد فيه من الجن والإنس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the hypocrites’ shayāṭīn are their chiefs and leaders.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد بشياطينهم كبراءهم وقادتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r5.claim: Maʿa joins one thing to another and is accusative like an adverb because ana maʿaka means I am settled with you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r5.anchor: (مع) كلمة تضم الشيء إلى الشيء، ونصبها كنصب الظروف؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r6.claim: Huzʾ means ridicule: the mocker outwardly shows something other than what is inward, to belittle and play around.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p169/r6.anchor: وهو أن يظهر غير ما يضمر استصغارا وعبثا (¬6)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:13-16/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:13-16/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:13-16/r2.claim: When alone with their leaders, they profess loyalty to their religion and say their public profession is mockery, displaying what they do not inwardly believe.

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r1.claim: When meeting believers the hypocrites say they believe, flatter those they consider foolish, and feign sincere loyalty.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r1.anchor: mü’minlere yaltaklanır, yüzden hulûskârlık, mürâîlik ederler

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r2.claim: Their 'satans' are rebellious, scheming teachers and leaders who make secret pacts and privately teach sedition and corruption; the hypocrites assure them they are allies.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r2.anchor: kendilerine gizli gizli fitne [237] ve fesad dersi veren

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r3.claim: They answer any concern about their dealings with believers by saying they are only mockers, proudly admitting treachery; these verses ground the general rule that contemptuous mockery of faith and doctrine entails unbelief.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r3.anchor: ilim ve akaidde istihfaf ve istihzânın mûcib-i küfr olması hakkındaki kā‘ide-i külliye bu gibi âyetlerin mazmûnudur

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r4.claim: One report says Abdullah b. Ubay went out with followers, called the approaching Companions fools, then welcomed Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali with lavish honorific praise before the verse was revealed.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r4.anchor: Rivayet olunduğuna göre Abdullah b. Übey yardaklarıyla bir gün sokağa çıkmışlar

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r5.claim: A fuller version says Ali rebuked Ibn Ubay, who claimed their faith matched the Muslims'; he then told his companions to act likewise, they praised him, and Muslims informed the Messenger before the verse descended.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r5.anchor: Müsaade et yâ Ebe’l-Hasen benim hakkımda böyle mi söylüyorsun? Vallahi bizim imanımız sizin imanınız gibi

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r6.claim: In that report, Ibn Ubay is the one who says 'we believe,' representing his companions; the earlier singular wording supports this reading.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r6.anchor: “âmennâ” diyen esasen İbn Übey b. Selûl oluyor ve bu sözle arkadaşlarını da temsil ediyor

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r7.claim: The plural satans are a group distinct from Ibn Ubay and the hypocrites, linked to them through a concealed organization; the verse reveals a deeper, hidden source of the incident.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r7.anchor: bu şeytanların gürûh-ı münâfıkīnin arkasında ve onlardan hâriç ve fakat onlarla gizli bir alâkayı hâiz hafî bir teşkilâta delâlet ettiği âşikârdır

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r8.claim: Many exegetes identify these satans beyond the hypocrite leaders as chiefs of the polytheists and Jewish scholars.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r8.anchor: birçok müfessirîn, bu şeyâtînin, reîs-i münâfıkīnden başka rüesâ-yı müşrikîne ve ahbâr-ı Yehûd’a işaret olduğunu nakletmişlerdir

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r9.claim: Shaytan is a common noun for any exceptionally rebellious, malicious creature, human or animal, visible or hidden; the hidden essence of human evil is known by its effects, and the term also applies to jinn and animals.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r9.anchor: insan şeytanında bile şeytanlık bir emr-i hafîdir

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r10.claim: Some philosophers explain the jinn Satan as only an immaterial spiritual being, but the author follows Ahl al-Sunna in also affirming its material aspect and evil material forces.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r10.anchor: bunun maddî haysiyetini de inkâr etmek doğru olamayacağından buna habis olan maddî kuvvetleri dahi ilâve etmek zarûrîdir. Ve ehl-i sünnetin îzahı böyledir

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r11.speaker: Sîbeveyh
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r11.claim: One etymology derives shaytan from sh-t-n, 'distance': Satan is far from truth and must be kept far away.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r11.anchor: Sîbeveyh’in dediği gibi uzaklık mânasına شطن maddesinden فَیْعَال veznindedir

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r12.claim: An alternative etymology derives shaytan from a root meaning burning or invalidation, on the fa'lan pattern; on this account it is not a proper name and is declinable.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r12.anchor: Diğeri ihtirak veya butlan mânasına شیط maddesinden فَعْلَاَن vezninde olmasıdır

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r13.claim: Shaytan is a genus name, especially for invisible evil spirits and powers; as every kind began with a first individual, it can evoke Iblis as the progenitor and function like a proper name.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r13.anchor: bu cinsin babası olan o ferd-i evvel, yani İblis hatıra gelir

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r14.claim: The Persian word for Satan is div, which the author says reached the West and became dieu with the opposite meaning, god.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r14.anchor: Şeytana lisân-ı Fârisîde “dîv” denilir ki bu kelime garba dolaşmış, aksine ilâh mânasına “dieu” olmuştur

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r15.claim: The author recounts that Umar dismounted a horse in Syria after it began prancing, saying they had put him on a satan; this illustrates that the term can literally describe an animal.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r15.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer Şam’a teşriflerinde bir ata bindirilmiş idi, biner binmez at çalım yapmaya başlayınca hemen inmiş

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r16.claim: Exegetes agree that the satans meant in this verse are human satans.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r16.anchor: Bu âyette ise insan şeytanları olduğunda müfessirînin ihtilâfı görülmüyor

ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r17.claim: The seventh verse succinctly summarizes the hypocrites' character and psychology, elaborating the opening description of them among people and compressing their whole spirit into two words of their own confession.
ELMALILI:2:13-15#2/r17.anchor: onların bütün rûhlarını kendi ikrarlarıyla iki kelimede hulâsa ederek gösterivermiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r1.claim: Attributing mockery, deception, and scheming to God means that He repays their agents in kind and makes their own traps ensnare them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r1.anchor: “Alay etmek, aldatmak, tuzaklara karşılık vermek” gibi fiillerin Allah’a nisbet edilmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r2.claim: Hypocrites think they hide their state and mock believers successfully, but God knows and informs the Prophet, making the hypocrites themselves objects of ridicule.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r2.anchor: gizli kameradan ekrana aktarılan kimseler gibi– kendilerini alay konusu haline getirmektedirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r4.claim: A person's life direction depends not only on personal reason, will, effort, and acquired knowledge, but also on education and guiding influences from the merciful or Satanic.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r4.anchor: İnsanoğlunun hayat çizgisini belirleyen âmiller yalnızca onun kendi akıl ve iradesi, kendi çabasıyla elde ettiği bilgiler değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r5.claim: Satan has helpers among jinn and human collaborators; the verse warns people to notice whom they accompany and whose influence they accept.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r5.anchor: Şeytanın cin türünden yardımcıları olduğu gibi insanlar arasından edindiği işbirlikçileri de vardır

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p21/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p21/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p21/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns Abdullah b. Ubayy and his companions: he warmly praised Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali before believers, then told his followers to imitate him and mock them; the Muslims reported this to the Prophet, and the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p21/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: نزلت هذه الآية في عبد الله بن أبي وأصحابه، وذلك أنهم خرجوا ذات يوم فاستقبلهم نفر من أصحاب رسول الله

QIRAAT-ER:2:14:18#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:14:18#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:14:18#1/r1.claim: The variant drops hamza from mustahziʾūn; the source calls it the most streamlined form and common in recitation traditions.
QIRAAT-ER:2:14:18#1/r1.anchor: Hamza dropped entirely (canonical in 10-reader system) — most streamlined form, common in recitation traditions

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p39#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p39#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p39#4/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the hypocrites’ ‘satans’ as the polytheists to whom they privately declare loyalty.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p39#4/r1.anchor: أنبأنا معمر بن قتادة في قوله ﴿ وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم ﴾ قال المشركون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r1.claim: Idha is chiefly a temporal adverb and usually conditional; al-Riyashi and al-Zajjaj treat surprise idha as temporal, while al-Mubarrad and the apparent Sibawayh view it as spatial, and the Kufans as a particle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r1.anchor: إذا: ظرف زمان، ويغلب كونها شرطا، وتقع للمفاجأة ظرف زمان وفاقا للرياشي، والزجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r2.claim: When a hollow triliteral past verb is passivized, Quraysh and Kinana use initial kasra and a silent y; other tribes use initial damma, with named readers distributed across these dialects, while a third dialect uses silent waw and is unattested in recitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r2.anchor: أخلص كسر أوله وسكنت عينه ياء في لغة قريش ومجاوريهم من بني كنانة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r5.claim: Innamā consists of mā that supports inna and prevents it from governing; it does not encode restriction by itself, which arises from context. Abu Hayyan rejects the claim that it combines affirmative inna with negative mā to create restriction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r5.anchor: والذي نذهب إليه أنها لا تدل على الحصر بالوضع، كما أن الحصر لا يفهم من أخواتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r6.claim: Some claim inna-mā is attested in governing constructions, but Abu Hayyan follows his school in judging such usage unattested in Arabic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p99/r6.anchor: وإعمال إنما قد زعم بعضهم أنه مسموع من لسان العرب، والذي عليه أصحابنا أنه غير مسموع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p100/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p100/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p100/r1.claim: Naḥnu is a detached nominative pronoun for a speaker together with others, or a speaker using the plural of majesty; grammarians discuss why it is built on ḍamma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p100/r1.anchor: نحن: ضمير رفع منفصل لمتكلم معه غيره أو لمعظم نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p101/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p101/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p101/r5.claim: Liqāʾ is meeting someone at close range; lāqā can function like the simple verb laqiya, and Arabic uses fourteen verbal nouns for meeting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p101/r5.anchor: اللقاء: استقبال الشخص قريبا منه، والفعل منه لقي يلقى، وقد يقال لاقى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p112/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p112/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p112/r5.claim: The plural pronoun wāw in laqū takes a vowel because a silent letter follows; the deleted root consonant does not return because this vowel is only temporary. Meeting can be planned or accidental, the latter termed coincidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p112/r5.anchor: والواو المضمومة في هذه القراءة هي واو الضمير تحركت لسكون ما بعدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r1.claim: Their unqualified amanna is deliberately ambiguous: they may make a false profession of belief in God and the Last Day, or mean only the outward words while their hearts turn away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r1.anchor: الإيمان المقيد في قولهم: آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر، وليسوا بصادقين في ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r2.claim: Most readers keep the wāw silent and pronounce the hamza in khalaw ilā; Warsh transfers the hamza vowel to wāw and deletes the hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: خلوا إلى بسكون الواو وتحقيق الهمزة، وقرأ ورش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r3.claim: Khalā takes either bi or ilā, but bi can mean withdrawing or mocking; ilā has a single endpoint sense and here implies directing their private meeting toward their devils. Abu al-Akhfash explains it as making them the goal of one's need.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r3.anchor: وعدل إلى إلى لأنها إذا عديت بالباء احتملت معنيين: أحدهما: الانفراد، والثاني: السخرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r4.speaker: النضر بن شميل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r4.claim: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and others say ilā can mean maʿa, as in two Qurʾanic examples; Abu Hayyan rejects those analogies and calls substitution of one preposition for another weak, contrary to Sibawayh and al-Khalil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r4.anchor: وزعم قوم، منهم النضر بن شميل: أن إلى هنا بمعنى مع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r5.claim: The devils are variously identified as Jews who ordered denial (Ibn Abbas), leaders in disbelief (Ibn Masud), jinn devils (a report from Ibn Abbas via al-Kalbi), or soothsayers (al-Dahhak and others); their name reflects rebellion, association with jinn, or their whispering and corrupting counsel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113/r5.anchor: وشياطينهم: هم اليهود الذين كانوا يأمرونهم بالتكذيب، قاله ابن عباس أو رؤساؤهم في الكفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r1.claim: Most readers vocalize the ʿayn in maʿakum; the anomalous inna maʿakum form reflects the dialect of Ghanm and Rabiʿa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r1.anchor: والجمهور على تحريك العين من معكم، وقرىء في الشاذ: إنا معكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r2.claim: To believers they say the bare verbal amannā, leaving it unconfirmed to imply a mere occurrence or avoid an implausible assertion; to their devils they use nominal innā maʿakum to assert settled loyalty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r2.anchor: فحين لقوا المؤمنين قالوا آمنا، أخبروا بالمطلق، كما تقدم، من غير توكيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r3.claim: Innamā nahnu mustahziʾūn is another emphatic nominal claim presenting mockery as their settled trait; they say their show of faith protects their lives, wealth, and families while they remain inwardly aligned with leaders.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r3.anchor: بل بينوا أن سبب مقالتهم للمؤمنين إنما هو الاستهزاء والاستخفاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r4.claim: The claim innā maʿakum may be spoken by hypocrites to their leaders or by all hypocrites to disbelievers; it answers the objection that they appear peaceful toward believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r4.anchor: والقائل إنا معكم، إما المنافقون لكبارهم، وإما كل المنافقين للكافرين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r5.claim: Mustahziʾūn is read with the hamza pronounced, softened between hamza and yāʾ according to Sibawayh, or fully changed to yāʾ according to Abu al-Hasan; some delete the yāʾ, though most readers follow Sibawayh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p113#2/r5.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه، رحمه الله، في تحقيقها: أن تجعل بين بين. ومذهب أبي الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p114/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p114/r1.claim: Four readings of being with the hypocrites' leaders are proposed: shared religion, assistance against the Prophet and Companions, sharing intelligence about believers, or joining in harming Muslims and suppressing God's message.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p114/r1.anchor: وهل الاجتماع والمعية في الدين، أو في النصرة والمعونة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p115/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p115/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p115/r1.claim: When meeting believers, hypocrites cannot conceal their dissimulation or participate in things believers dislike, so they outwardly show submission and obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p115/r1.anchor: إذا لقوهم قالوا آمنا، فهم عند لقائهم لا يستطيعون إظهار المداراة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r5.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r5.claim: One reported occasion is that these verses were revealed about hypocrites generally.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r6.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r6.claim: A second view says God described a people before they existed, thereby disclosing unseen knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r6.anchor: في قوم أعلم الله بوصفهم قبل وجودهم، وفيه إعلام بالمغيبات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r7.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r7.claim: A third view places the meeting verse in the story of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and his companions, while the preceding passage concerns hypocrites generally; he praised Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAlī to believers, then told his companions he had turned them away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r7.anchor: في عبد الله بن أبي وأصحابه نزل: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا والتي قبلها في جميع المنافقين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r1.claim: The verse explains the hypocrites' habit: when meeting believers they profess faith to fend them off; this adds their mockery, guile, and situational motive rather than repeating the opening description.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r1.anchor: بيان لدأب المنافقين وأنهم إذا أستقبلوا المؤمنين دفعوهم عن أنفسهم بقولهم آمنا إستهزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r2.claim: The Imam distinguishes the first profession as beginning faith and this one as sincerity; al-Alusi rejects this because their verbal confession was already known and the proposed distinction lacks support.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r2.anchor: والقول بأن المراد ب ( آمنا ) أولا الأخبار عن إحداث الإيمان وهنا عز إحداث إخلاص الإيمان مما أرتضاه الإمام ولا أقتدي به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r3.claim: Liqāʾ means meeting someone face-to-face nearby and is one of fourteen verbal nouns of laqiya; Abū Ḥanīfa and Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ read lāqaw, which al-Baḥr treats as the simple verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r3.anchor: واللقاء إستقبال الشخص قريبا منه وهو أحد أربعة عشر مصدرا للقى وقرأ أبو حنيفة وإبن السميقع لاقوا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r4.claim: The object of 'we believe' is omitted either because the preceding passage specified belief in God and the Last Day or because it means belief in what the believers believe; the proposed Moses-only reading is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r4.anchor: حذف المفعول في آمنا قيل إكتفاء بالتقييد قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r5.claim: No sound occasion-of-revelation report is known to al-Alusi; he rejects accounts passed through al-Suddī al-ṣaghīr, whom he calls a liar, and dismisses that chain as fabricated.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r5.anchor: ولم يصح عندي في سبب نزول هذه الآية شيء وأما ما ذكره الزمخشري والبيضاوي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r6.claim: Khaliyā ilayhim means they were alone with their leaders; the omitted first object is understood, while ilā conveys moving away from one thing toward another. The phrase also recalls the idiom 'seek the matter, your blame is past'.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r6.anchor: من خلوت به وإليه إذا أنفردت معه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r7.claim: Reading khalaw as 'they mocked them in private' is unsuitable: no trusted attestation gives khalā that explicit meaning, and the idiom about playing with someone's honor can retain its literal or 'gain power over' sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r7.anchor: وإحتمال أن يكون من خلوت به اي سخرت منه فمعنى الآية إذا أنهوا السخرية معهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r8.speaker: النضر بن شميل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r8.claim: Al-Naḍr b. Shumayl claims ilā here means maʿa, 'with'; al-Alusi says there is no evidence for this or for treating the preposition as a substitute for biʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r8.anchor: وزعم النضر بن شميل أن ( إلى ) هنا بمعنى مع ولا دليل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r9.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r9.claim: Al-Rāghib understands the root khalw as a place, space, or time being empty of an occupant; al-Alusi notes that taking it to mean 'pass away' is then figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p156#2/r9.anchor: ويفهم من كلام الراغب أن أصل معنى الخلو فراغ المكان والحيز عن شاغل وكذا الزمان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the hypocrites' 'satans' as the people who instructed them to deny the truth, identified here as Jews.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r1.anchor: من كانوا يأمرونهم بالتكذيب من اليهودكما قاله إبن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and a group identify their satans as soothsayers, named for rebellion and for making evil seem good and good seem evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r2.anchor: أو كهنتهم كما قاله الضحاك وجماعة وسموا بذلك لتمردهم وتحسينهم القبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī takes the satans to be jinn; al-Alusi says this interpretation does not occur to him as plausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r3.anchor: وحمله على شياطين الجن كما قاله الكلبي مما لا يختلج بقلبي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r4.claim: If the referents are soothsayers, their jinn companions may explain the name; al-Alusi lists several soothsayers active in the Prophet's era, including Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf and Abū Burda.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r4.anchor: وكان على عهده صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كثير منهم ككعب بن الأشرف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r5.claim: Shayāṭīn is a broken plural, though a rare anomalous reading treats it like a sound masculine plural, tanazzalat bihi al-shayāṭūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r5.anchor: والشياطين جمع تكسير وإجراؤه مجرى الصحيح كما في بعض الشواذ تنزلت به الشياطون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r6.speaker: البصريون
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r6.claim: The Basran derivation makes shayṭān a fayʿāl with a radical nūn, from shatana, 'to be far away,' because Satan is distant from obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r6.anchor: والمفرد شيطان وهو فيعال عند البصريين فنونه أصلية من شطن أي بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r7.speaker: الكوفيون
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r7.claim: The Kufans derive shayṭān as faʿlān, with an added nūn, from shāṭa, meaning to perish, fail, or burn with anger.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r7.anchor: وعند الكوفيين وزنه فعلان فنونه زائدة من شاط يشيط إذا هلك أو بطل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r8.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās defines a shayṭān broadly as any rebel among jinn, humans, or animals.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157/r8.anchor: وروى عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن الشيطان كل متمرد من الجن والإنس والدواب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r1.claim: Their 'we are with you' denotes spiritual alliance: sharing their leaders' Judaism, described as the root of evils.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r1.anchor: قالوا إنا معكم أي معية معنوية وهي مسواتهم لهم في إعتقاد اليهودية وهو أم الخبائث

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r2.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the contrast in form: a nonassertive verbal clause to believers feigning a new act of faith, but an emphatic nominal clause to leaders to claim lasting allegiance and forestall their doubts.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r2.anchor: وعندي أن الوجه هو الأول إذ يرد على الأخيرين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r3.claim: An alternative says they assert themselves with leaders because they sincerely wish to reassure them, whereas they withhold assertion when speaking to believers because they do not care about them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r3.anchor: إن التأكيد كما يكون لأزالة الإنكار والشك يكون لصدق الرغبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is that they avoid claiming full, settled faith before perceptive believers, while their leaders would accept such a claim; al-Alusi finds this and the desire-based account unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r4.anchor: أو لأنهم لو قالوا إنا مؤمنون كان إدعاء لكمال الإيمان وثباته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r5.claim: The hypocrites may assert allegiance to leaders to claim eligibility for the believers' legal treatment and protection from conflict; they had already used an oath by God and the Last Day to deceive believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r5.anchor: إنهم للتقية والخداع ودعوى أنهم مثل المؤمنين في الإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r6.claim: The majority read maʿakum with a vowel on ʿayn; a rare reading with sukūn is dialectal among Rabīʿa and Ghanm.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ( معكم ) بتحريك العين وقريء شاذا بسكونها وهي لغة ربيعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r7.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r7.claim: Al-Ghazālī defines mockery as contempt and pointing out defects in a laughable way, which may be done through mimicry, speech, gesture, or sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r7.anchor: وذكر حجة الإسلام الغزالي أن الإستهزاء الإستحقار والإستهانة والتنبيه على العيوب والنقائص

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r8.claim: Al-Alusi rejects al-Rāzī's definition of mockery as outwardly showing agreement while inwardly carrying its opposite, because it conflicts with language and common usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r8.anchor: وقول الرازي إنه عبارة عن إظهار موافقة مع إبطال ما يجري مجرى السوء على طريق السخرية غير موافق للغة والعرف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r9.claim: The last clause may be a resumption answering the leaders' implied question about why the hypocrites associate with believers; alternatively it is a badal, confirmation, or explanation of the necessary implication of allegiance. The learned prefer resumption, though innamā makes an implied question less likely.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r9.anchor: وأولى الأوجه عند المحققين الإستئناف لولا ما ذكره الشيخ في دلائل الأعجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r10.claim: The final word has rare readings that lighten the hamza or replace it with a yāʾ; some omit the yāʾ and give the zāy a ḍamma.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p157#2/r10.anchor: وقريء ( مستهزؤن ) بتخفيف الهمزة وبقلبها ياء مضمونة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r1.claim: The opening explains the hypocrites' dealings with believers and disbelievers, advancing their doctrine and preparing the account of hypocrisy rather than repeating an earlier statement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r1.anchor: بيان لمعاملتهم المؤمنين والكفار، وما صدرت به القصة فمساقه لبيان مذهبهم وتمهيد نفاقهم فليس بتكرير.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r2.claim: A report says Ibn Ubayy staged lavish greetings for Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali before Companions to show his people how he would turn these supposed fools away; the verse was then revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r2.anchor: روي أن ابن أبي وأصحابه استقبلهم نفر من الصحابة، فقال لقومه:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r3.claim: Liqāʾ means encountering or meeting; ilqāʾ derives from throwing because throwing places an object where it will meet something.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14/r3.anchor: واللقاء المصادفة يقال؛ لقيته ولاقيته، إذا صادفته واستقبلته، ومنه ألقيته إذا طرحته

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r1.claim: Khalaw ilayhi may mean withdrawing privately with someone, turning away from him, or mocking him; ilayhi reflects the sense of reaching an end.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r1.anchor: من خلوت بفلان وإليه إذا انفردت معه. أو من خلاك ذم أي عداك ومضى عنك، ومنه القرون الخالية.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r2.claim: Their satans are openly disbelieving rebels like Satan, joined to the hypocrites by shared disbelief; alternatively they are senior hypocrites while the speakers are juniors.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بشياطينهم الذين ماثلوا الشيطان في تمردهم، وهم المظهرون كفرهم، وإضافتهم إليهم للمشاركة في الكفر. أو كبار المنافقين والقائلون صغارهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r3.speaker: سيبويه
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r3.claim: Sibawayh analyzes the nūn in shayṭān as original, deriving it from distance and remoteness from good, supported by tashayṭana; he also analyzes it as extra, from shāṭa, to perish.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r3.anchor: وجعل سيبويه نونه تارة أصلية على أنه من شطن إذا بعد فإنه بعيد عن الصلاح، ويشهد له قولهم: تشيطن. وأخرى زائدة على أنه من شاط إذا بطل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r4.claim: They tell believers in a verbal clause that faith has newly begun, but tell their satans in an emphatic nominal clause that their allegiance is stable; they lack sincere belief and would not persuade the Companions of perfect faith.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#2/r4.anchor: خاطبوا المؤمنين بالجملة الفعلية، والشياطين بالجملة الإسمية المؤكدة بإن لأنهم قصدوا بالأولى دعوى إحداث الإيمان

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#3/r1.claim: Their claim to be mockers may emphasize the preceding statement, replace it, or answer an imagined challenge from their satans about why they join believers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#3/r1.anchor: تأكيد لما قبله، لأن المستهزىء بالشيء المستخف به مصر على خلافه. أو بدل منه لأن من حقر الإسلام فقد عظم الكفر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#3/r2.claim: Istihzāʾ means mockery or belittlement; the root suggests lightness, rapid killing, and a camel moving swiftly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:14#3/r2.anchor: والاستهزاء السخرية والاستخفاف يقال: هزئت واستهزأت بمعنى كأجبت واستجبت، وأصله الخفة من الهزء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r1.claim: At Uhud, Qazman fought fiercely although the Prophet said he belonged to the people of Hell; wounded, he said he fought only for tribal zeal, then severed his hand and died.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r1.anchor: ومأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إنه من أهل النار , فجرح فبشر بالجنة فقال : واللهما قاتلت إلاحمية لقومي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r2.claim: The passage names al-Jadd ibn Qays, who asked to be excused lest he be tempted, and identifies Ibn Ubayy as the head of the hypocrites who gathered around him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r2.anchor: والجد بن قيس وهو الذي قال : ( ائذن لي ولاتفتني ) وعبد الله بن أبي رأس المنافقين وإليه كانوا يجتمعون

BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r3.claim: The author associates Wadiʿa al-ʿAwfi, Malik ibn Abi Fawqal, Suwayd, and Daʿis with Ibn Ubayy's group and cites the revelation about hypocrites siding with their disbelieving scripture-community brothers.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p41/r3.anchor: وفيه وفي وديعة العوفي ومالك بن أبي فوقل وسويد وداعس وهم من رهطه نزل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r8.claim: The past-tense form آمنا suffices to convey the hypocrites' claim that they believe, even if the belief arose only as a transient act.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r8.anchor: معبرين بالجملة الفعلية الماضية التي يكفي في إفادتها لما سقيت له أدنى الحدوث

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r9.claim: A meeting entails some turning toward one another; believers whose faith is an established attribute rarely meet hypocrites in a way that permits intimacy or speech.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r10.claim: The hypocrites' private return to their leaders is expressed as going to their devils; Satan is one profoundly distant from the place of good.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r10.anchor: الذين هم رؤوسهم من غير أن يكون معهم مؤمن , والشيطان هو الذي الشديد البعد عن محل الخير

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r11.claim: Their nominal statement إنّا معكم, reinforced by emphasis, presents their allegiance as fixed and counters any suspicion that their public compliance changed their position.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r11.anchor: معبرين بالأسمة الدالة على الثبات مؤكدين لها دالالة على نشاطهم لهذا الإخبار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r12.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r12.claim: They explain their gentleness toward believers by saying they are only mocking: mockery displays seriousness while concealing its joking intent.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r12.anchor: الهزء إظهار الجد وإخفاء الهزل فيه قاله الحرالي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r13.claim: God's mockery repays theirs through gradual enticement: they are treated outwardly as believers while being made to taste renewed humiliation in both worlds.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r13.anchor: يجازهم على فعلهم بالاستداج بأن يظهر لهم من أمره المرذي لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r14.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r14.claim: The imperfect verb for God's mockery indicates renewed, continuing recompense; its verbal form also leaves room for repentance by one who repents.

DURR-FULL:v1p77/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p77/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p77/r3.claim: The verse was revealed about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions; he ostentatiously praised Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAli to believers, then told his allies to praise him for it.
DURR-FULL:v1p77/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت هذه الآية في عبد الله بن أبي وأصحابه

DURR-FULL:v1p77/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p77/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p77/r4.claim: Some Jews told the Prophet's Companions they shared their religion, then privately assured their allies they remained with them and were mocking Muhammad's followers.
DURR-FULL:v1p77/r4.anchor:
عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا} الآية
قال: كان رجال من اليهود إذا لقوا أصحاب النبي

DURR-FULL:v1p77/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p77/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p77/r6.claim: A report identifies them as hypocrites among the People of the Book who told their own people they remained on their religion while mocking Muhammad's Companions.
DURR-FULL:v1p77/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا} وهم منافقو أهل الكتاب

NASHR:v1p396/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p396/r1.speaker: الأصبهاني عن ورش
NASHR:v1p396/r1.claim: Al-Asbahani transmits Warsh’s hamza replacement in several listed forms and adds replacement in فبأي when preceded by ف; bare بأي forms are treated separately.
NASHR:v1p396/r1.anchor: وافقه الأصبهاني عن ورش في (خاسيا) ، و (ناشية) و (مليت) وزاد فأبدل (فبأي)

NASHR:v1p396/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p396/r2.speaker: الحمامي وصاحب المبهج
NASHR:v1p396/r2.claim: Al-Hammami reports replacement in bare بأي from both transmitters; al-Mubhij reports both replacement and verification for بأيكم المفتون, while other Hibat Allah routes verify.
NASHR:v1p396/r2.anchor: فروى الحمامي من جميع طرقه، عن هبة الله والمطوعي كلاهما عنه إبدال الهمزة فيها

NASHR:v1p396/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p396/r3.speaker: أبو العلاء الحافظ
NASHR:v1p396/r3.claim: Al-Abu al-Ala uniquely transmits replacement in شانيك from al-Nahrawani.
NASHR:v1p396/r3.anchor: وانفرد أبو العلاء الحافظ عن النهرواني بالإبدال في (شانيك)

NASHR:v1p396/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p396/r4.speaker: الهذلي
NASHR:v1p396/r4.claim: Al-Hudhali uniquely reports replacement in لنبوينهم in al-Kamil.
NASHR:v1p396/r4.anchor: وانفرد الهذلي في " الكامل " بالإبدال في (لنبوينهم)

NASHR:v1p396/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p396/r5.speaker: ابن مهران والأزرق عن ورش
NASHR:v1p396/r5.claim: Ibn Mihran omits replacement from his account of al-Asbahani, against other transmitters; al-Azraq uniquely changes the hamza to yāʾ in لئلا in al-Baqara, al-Nisa, and al-Hadid.
NASHR:v1p396/r5.anchor: وانفرد ابن مهران عن الأصبهاني فلم يذكر له إبدالا في هذا الحال، فخالف سائر الناس

NASHR:v1p396/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p396/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v1p396/r6.claim: When a dammated hamza follows kasra before waw, Abu Jaafar deletes it and dammats the preceding letter, as in مستهزون.
NASHR:v1p396/r6.anchor: فإن أبا جعفر يحذف الهمزة ويضم ما قبلها من أجل الواو نحو (مستهزون

NASHR:v1p396/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p396/r8.speaker: ابن وردان
NASHR:v1p396/r8.claim: Ibn Wardan differs over المنشئون: several routes report hamza and others deletion; Ibn al-Jazari says both forms are sound, and Ibn Jammaz consistently deletes.
NASHR:v1p396/r8.anchor: ونص له على الخلاف أبو طاهر بن سوار، والوجهان عنه صحيحان، ولم يختلف عن ابن جماز في حذفه

NASHR:v1p396/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p396/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p396/r9.claim: Authorities differ on whether the deletion rule includes نبيوني، أنبيوني، يتكيون، يستنبونك; al-Ahwazi and others specify them, while al-Az and al-Hudhali appear to generalize it.
NASHR:v1p396/r9.anchor: وظاهر كلام أبي العز والهذلي العموم، على أن الأهوازي وغيره نص عليها، ولا يظهر فرق سوى الرواية

NASHR:v1p441/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p441/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p441/r1.claim: One described method transfers the hamza’s vowel to the preceding letter, which then takes damma, fatha, or kasra according to the examples.
NASHR:v1p441/r1.anchor: فتضم في نحو (ومنهم أميون) وتفتح في نحو (أنتم أعلم) وتكسر في نحو (إيمانكم إن كنتم)

NASHR:v1p441/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p441/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p441/r2.claim: A second method dammats the preceding letter in every case, avoiding a mīm with a nonoriginal vowel.
NASHR:v1p441/r2.anchor: أنها تضم مطلقا، ولو كانت الهمزة مفتوحة أو مكسورة حذرا من تحرك الميم بغير حركتها الأصلية

NASHR:v1p441/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p441/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p441/r3.claim: A third method transfers the vowel for damma and kasra but not fatha, to avoid confusion with the dual.
NASHR:v1p441/r3.anchor: ينقل في الضم والكسر دون الفتح لئلا تشتبه بالتثنية

NASHR:v1p441/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p441/r4.speaker: بعض النحاة
NASHR:v1p441/r4.claim: Some grammarians allow a final hamza after a sound consonant to be replaced at pause by a letter matching the vowel before that consonant.
NASHR:v1p441/r4.anchor: وأجاز بعض النحاة في الساكن الصحيح قبل الهمز المتطرف إبدال الهمزة بمثل حركة ما قبل ذلك الساكن حالة الوقف

NASHR:v1p441/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p441/r5.speaker: أبو العلاء
NASHR:v1p441/r5.claim: Abu al-Ala alone among the readers reports a further form for الخبء: transfer followed by replacing the hamza with alif when it is fatha.
NASHR:v1p441/r5.anchor: ولم يوافق على هذا أحد من القراء إلا الحافظ أبو العلاء، فإنه حكى وجها آخر في (الخبء) تبدل الهمزة ألفا بعد النقل

NASHR:v1p441/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p441/r6.speaker: ابن مالك
NASHR:v1p441/r6.claim: Grammarians also allow transferring only to the preceding consonant; Ibn Malik treats that pattern as regular in his Tashil, but no reader adopts it.
NASHR:v1p441/r6.anchor: وأجاز بعضهم في نحو هذا أيضا النقل إلى الحرف فقط، فيقول: هذا الخبؤ والدفؤ والجزؤ

NASHR:v1p441/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p441/r7.speaker: الكوفيون
NASHR:v1p441/r7.claim: Kufan grammarians analogize transfer and hamza-to-alif replacement from كمأة to forms such as يسألون and النشأة; no reader agrees except Abu al-Ala al-Hamdani, with النشأة also singled out by some.
NASHR:v1p441/r7.anchor: وقاس عليه الكوفيون، فيجيزون (يسألون ويجأرون والنشأة) وحركة الساكن بالفتح في ذلك هي حركة الهمزة

NASHR:v1p441/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p441/r8.speaker: الفراء وأبو زيد
NASHR:v1p441/r8.claim: They report an Arabic pattern that builds the word on its verb form after changing hamza to yāʾ, yielding forms such as مستهزون and يستهزون.
NASHR:v1p441/r8.anchor: وروى الفراء وأبو زيد ذلك عن العرب. فمن أبدل منهم الهمزة في الفعل قال

NASHR:v1p443/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p443/r1.speaker: الزجاج
NASHR:v1p443/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains يستهزون as the regular dialect that changes hamza to yāʾ in the verb استهزأ, and applies the same account to related forms.
NASHR:v1p443/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: أما (يستهزون) فعلى لغة من يبدل من الهمزة ياء في الأصل، فيقولون في (استهزأ: استهزيت)

NASHR:v1p443/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p443/r3.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v1p443/r3.claim: Several routes report Hamza pausing on مستهزون without hamza and with raised zāy; al-Jazari accepts this as a sound, well-attested performance.
NASHR:v1p443/r3.anchor: عن حمزة أنه كان يقف (مستهزون) بغير همز ويضم الزاي

NASHR:v1p443/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p443/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p443/r4.claim: Al-Jazari rejects al-Sakhawi and al-Fasi’s claim that the raised-vowel deletion form is weak: the poem’s final alif marks length, and the form is among Hamza’s strongest pause readings.
NASHR:v1p443/r4.anchor: (قلت) : وهذا نص صريح بهذا الوجه مع صحته في القياس والأداء، والعجب من أبي الحسن السخاوي

NASHR:v1p443/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p443/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p443/r5.claim: The weak form is deletion of hamza while retaining kasra before waw; al-Jazari distinguishes it from the sound raised-vowel pause form.
NASHR:v1p443/r5.anchor: وإنما الخامل الوجه الآخر، وهو حذف الهمزة وإبقاء ما قبل الواو مكسورا على

NASHR:v1p274/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274/r1.speaker: الهذلي عن الهاشمي عن ابن جماز
NASHR:v1p274/r1.claim: Al-Hudhali uniquely reports no ṣila for Ibn Jammaz in any context, except when a hamzat al-qatʿ follows the plural mīm.
NASHR:v1p274/r1.anchor: وانفرد الهذلي عن الهاشمي عن ابن جماز بعدم الصلة مطلقا كيف وقعت، إلا أنه مقيد بما لم يكن قبل همز قطع

NASHR:v1p274/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274/r2.speaker: ورش
NASHR:v1p274/r2.claim: Warsh joins the ṣila when hamzat al-qatʿ follows plural mīm, including معكم إنما; the other readers keep the mīm still throughout the Quran.
NASHR:v1p274/r2.anchor: ووافق ورشا على الصلة إذا وقع بعد ميم الجمع همزة قطع نحو (عليهم أأنذرتهم أم) (معكم إنما)

NASHR:v1p274/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v1p274/r3.claim: When a still follows plural mīm preceded by hāʾ after kasra or yāʾ, Abu Amr reads both mīm and hāʾ with kasra.
NASHR:v1p274/r3.anchor: فكسر الميم والهاء في ذلك كله أبو عمرو وضم الميم وكسر الهاء نافع

NASHR:v1p274/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274/r4.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم وأبو جعفر
NASHR:v1p274/r4.claim: For the same environment, these readers damma the mīm and kasra the hāʾ.
NASHR:v1p274/r4.anchor: وضم الميم وكسر الهاء نافع، وابن كثير، وابن عامر، وعاصم وأبو جعفر

NASHR:v1p274/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
NASHR:v1p274/r5.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf damma both the plural mīm and the preceding hāʾ in that environment.
NASHR:v1p274/r5.anchor: وضم الميم والهاء جميعا حمزة، والكسائي، وخلف

NASHR:v1p274/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274/r6.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v1p274/r6.claim: Yaqub matches the plural mīm to the hāʾ’s own vowel: he dammas it after a dammated hāʾ and kasras it after a kasra.
NASHR:v1p274/r6.anchor: وأتبع يعقوب الميم الهاء على أصله المتقدم، فضمها حيث ضم الهاء وكسرها حيث كسرها

NASHR:v1p274/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274/r7.speaker: رويس
NASHR:v1p274/r7.claim: At pause all readers still the plural mīm; the hāʾ follows each reader’s principles, while Ruways retains both options in يغنهم الله.
NASHR:v1p274/r7.anchor: وأما حكم الوقف فكلهم على إسكان الميم، وهي في الهاء على أصولهم

NASHR:v1p274/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p274/r8.claim: Readers agree on damma for plural mīm when the preceding letter is dammated, but still the mīm at pause.
NASHR:v1p274/r8.anchor: وأجمعوا على ضم الميم إذا كان قبلها ضم، سواء كان هاء أم كافا أم تاء

IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r7.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r7.claim: Their satans are Jews who urge the hypocrites to deny the truth and oppose what the Messenger brought.
IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r7.anchor: من يهود، الذين يأمرونهم بالتكذيب بالحق، وخلاف ما جاء به الرسول

IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r8.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r8.claim: Their assurance to their satans means that they share the same position as them.
IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r8.anchor: أي إنا على مثل ما أنتم عليه

IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r9.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r9.claim: They say they are only mocking and playing with the believers.
IBNHISHAM:v1p531#2/r9.anchor: أي إنما نستهزئ بالقوم، ونلعب بهم

IBNHISHAM:v2p547/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p547/r2.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v2p547/r2.claim: A private confidant is someone secretly trusted apart from God; Ibn Hisham compares this concealed allegiance to hypocrites who publicly profess faith but privately tell their satans they are with them.
IBNHISHAM:v2p547/r2.anchor: نحو ما يصنع المنافقون، يظهرون الإيمان للذين آمنوا وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم قالوا إنا معكم

BURHAN:v4p70/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p70/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p70/r3.claim: When they return to their satans, they report their own steadfast allegiance to them.
BURHAN:v4p70/r3.anchor: يخبرون عن انفسهم بالثبات على الايمان بهم

ITQAN:v2p434/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p434/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p434/r1.claim: إذا can describe an enduring pattern across past, present, and future, like the imperfect; here it means this is their constant conduct.
ITQAN:v2p434/r1.anchor: قد تستعمل إذا للاستمرار في الأحوال الماضية والحاضرة والمستقبلة كما يستعمل الفعل المضارع لذلك

DAMGHANI:v1p263/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p263/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p263/r4.claim: The hypocrites’ shayāṭīn are their soothsayers, including Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf and others.
DAMGHANI:v1p263/r4.anchor: فوجه منها : الشياطين الكهنة قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

DAMGHANI:v1p436/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p436/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p436/r6.claim: In 2:14, maʿakum means that the hypocrites share their leaders’ religion; the same use appears of those with Hud and of the speaker’s companions.
DAMGHANI:v1p436/r6.anchor: فوجه منها : معكم اى عى دينكم . قوله تعالى فى سورة البقرة

BURHAN:v3p354/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.claim: The four broken plural forms of paucity and the two sound plurals are inherently paucity forms; other plurals may indicate few or many as context determines, as Qur'anic examples show.
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.anchor: واعلم أن جموع التكثير الأربعة وجمعى التصحيح أعنى جمع التأنيث وجمع التذكير كل ذلك للقلة

BURHAN:v1p108/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p108/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p108/r2.claim: Shayṭān generally means Iblīs, his followers, and descendants; in shayāṭīnihim it means their soothsayers, including Kaʿb al-Ashraf, Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab, and his brother Abū Yāsir.
BURHAN:v1p108/r2.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن من ذكر شيطان فإنه إبليس وجنوده وذريته إلا قوله تعالى فى سورة البقرة ﴿ وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم ﴾

BURHAN:v4p104/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p104/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p104/r2.claim: The rhetoricians say no conjunction is needed when a following clause is so closely joined that it restates or emphasizes the first, as predicate, explanation or equivalent meaning.
BURHAN:v4p104/r2.anchor: وقال البيانيون للجملة ثلاثة أحوال فالاول إن يكون ما قبلها بمنزلة الصفة من الموصوف والتاكيد من المؤكد فلا يدخلها عطف

BURHAN:v3p339/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p339/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p339/r4.claim: خلوا إلى is better explained by embedding the sense 'went off' or 'departed,' parallel to لقوا, than by claiming إلى means باء or مع.
BURHAN:v3p339/r4.anchor: لكن ضمن خلوا معنى ذهبوا وانصرفوا

BURHAN:v3p339/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p339/r5.speaker: مكي
BURHAN:v3p339/r5.claim: Makki says إلى avoids the ambiguity of خلوت به, which can mean that someone mocked the person.
BURHAN:v3p339/r5.anchor: وقال مكي إنما لم تأت الباء لأنه يقال خلوت به إذا سخرت منه فأتى ب إلى لدفع هذا الوهم

ITQAN:v2p418/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p418/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v2p418/r4.claim: Shayṭān normally refers to Iblīs and his hosts, but 'their satans' means the hypocrites' human ringleaders.
ITQAN:v2p418/r4.anchor: وكل شيطان فيه فإبليس وجنوده إلا ﴿ وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم ﴾

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p181#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p181#2/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p181#2/r3.claim: If they said ‘we are only mockers’ merely to evade their leaders’ harm, without intending mockery, those words alone would not warrant blame; culpability depends on intent and feigned faith.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p181#2/r3.anchor: لكان لا يكون عليهم مؤاخذة فيما قالوه من حيث كانت المؤاخذة تكون على اعتقاد الاستهزاء والخديعة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r6.claim: Reciprocal terms such as mock, scheme, evil, and aggression name God's requital: the first aggression is injustice, while the answering act is just punishment.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r6.anchor: إنما نحن مستهزؤن (14) الله يستهزئ بهم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r1.claim: The hypocrites use a verbal clause for their claim to believers but an emphatic nominal clause to assure their own faction of lasting allegiance.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r1.anchor: فقد فَرَّقَ بين قولهم للمؤمنين وقولهم لأصحابهم فقد خاطبوا المؤمنين بالجملة الفعلية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r2.claim: One possible reason they avoid calling themselves believers is that their beliefs give them no inward motive to say it sincerely.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r2.anchor: إمّا لأن أنفسهم لا تساعدهم عليه إذ ليس لهم من عقائدهم باعثٌ ومُحَرِّكٌ

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the nominal assurance fits their settled Judaism and disbelief, which they gladly affirm and their own group accepts as genuine.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r3.anchor: من الثبات على اليهودية والقرار على اعتقاد الكفر والبعد من أن يزلوا عنه
